In fine autem mundi omnes ubique convertentur, et ita dicentur filii Dei, fide recepta, qui antea dicebantur filii diaboli.
paras.en: According to this diversity, what follows is also explained in different ways. For there is added: [[1:10|And it shall be in the place|Et erit in loco]] (that is, what follows shall come to pass), that is, in Jerusalem and the places near it, [[1:10|where it shall be said to them|ubi dicetur eis]], that is, where God said to the Jews through the Prophets, [[1:10|You are not my people|Non populus meus estis vos]], when you worshipped idols (for this the Lord often said to this people through Jeremias), [[1:10|it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis estis]]: that is, there, after their conversion, they shall be called the adopted sons of the living and true God, from whom as from a fountain flows all the life of nature, the life of grace and the life of glory. For when Christ became incarnate and lived and preached among the Jews, many believed in Him, and many more were converted by the Apostles of Christ after the sending of the Paraclete. Others understand by this place the whole world, in which the Jews have been dispersed, and many of them have already been converted to Christ. But at the end of the world all everywhere will be converted, and so, having received the faith, they will be called sons of God, who before were called sons of the devil.

paras.t: Et congregabuntur filii Juda, id est nati de tribu Juda, Levi ac Benjamin, qui per Judam designantur, quoniam reges erant de tribu Juda, et filii Israel, id est aliqui nati de decem tribubus, pariter, corporaliter vel spiritualiter. Et ponent sibimet caput unum, id est, in Christum concorditer credent: quod universaliter implebitur per prædicationem Enoch atque Eliæ, qui sicut in Evangelio scriptum est, restituet omnia. Et ascendent de terra, id est, cœlestia quærent, et ad divina consurgent, quemadmodum monet Apostolus: Quæ sursum sunt quærite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei; quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram. Porro hæc fient, quoniam magnus dies Jezrael. Jezrael interpretatur semen Dei: per quod intelligi potest Christus, de quo legitur, In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes; vel congregatio fidelium. Est itaque sensus, quod magnus est dies Christi, id est tempus gratiæ, quia in eo Christus magnifice fecit nobiscum, maximam gratiam tribuendo, totumque mundum illustrando, adversarios humanæ salutis dejiciendo, et infinita mirabilia perpetrando. Magnus est quoque dies Ecclesiæ, quæ in nomine Christi mirabilia operatur, et a Sole justitiæ gratiosissime illustratur. De hoc die fertur in Psalmo: Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus.
paras.en: [[1:11|And the children of Juda|filii Juda]] (that is, those born of the tribe of Juda, Levi and Benjamin, who are signified by Juda, since the kings were of the tribe of Juda) [[1:11|and the children of Israel|et filii Israel]] (that is, some born of the ten tribes) [[1:11|shall be gathered|Et congregabuntur]] [[1:11|together|pariter]], bodily or spiritually. [[1:11|and they shall appoint themselves one head|Et ponent sibimet caput unum]]: that is, they shall believe in Christ with one accord; which will be fulfilled universally through the preaching of Enoch and Elias, who, as is written in the Gospel, shall [[Matt 17:11|restore all things|restituet omnia]]. [[1:11|and shall come up out of the land|Et ascendent de terra]]: that is, they shall seek heavenly things and rise up to things divine, as the Apostle admonishes: [[Col 3:1|seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God|Quæ sursum sunt quærite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei]]; [[Col 3:2|Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth|quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram]]. Now these things shall come to pass, [[1:11|for great is the day of Jezrahel|quoniam magnus dies Jezrael]]. Jezrael is interpreted "seed of God": by which may be understood Christ, of whom we read: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes]][[Gen 12:3||]][[Gen 26:4||]]; or the congregation of the faithful. The sense, then, is that great is the day of Christ, that is, the time of grace, because in it Christ has done great things with us, bestowing the greatest grace, enlightening the whole world, casting down the adversaries of man's salvation, and working countless wonders. Great too is the day of the Church, which works wonders in the name of Christ and is most graciously enlightened by the Sun of justice. Of this day it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 117:24|This is the day which the Lord hath made|Hæc est dies quam fecit Dominus]].

paras.t: Verumtamen expositiones istæ infirmantur per hoc, quod Apostolus ad Romanos allegat præinductam scripturam de vocatione gentium prænuntiatam. Sic etenim ait sanctus Apostolus: Deus sustinuit in multa patientia vasa iræ apta in interitum, ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ in vasa misericordiæ. Quos et vocavit, non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus, sicut in Osee dicit: Vocabo non plebem meam, plebem meam; et non misericordiam consecutam, misericordiam consecutam; et erit in loco ubi dictum est eis, Non plebs mea vos; ibi vocabuntur filii Dei vivi. Sequendo ergo intellectum divini Apostoli, advertendum quod Prophetæ et Apostoli eodem Spiritu docti atque locuti sunt. Quemadmodum ergo in novo Testamento fit distinctio inter Judæos, seu Israel, carnales et spirituales (de carnali siquidem dicit Apostolus, Videte Israel secundum carnem; Joannes quoque in Apocalypsi, Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ; de spirituali vero loquitur Paulus, Pax super eos, et super Israel Dei); sic Prophetæ loquuntur de duplici Israele, puta carnali ac spirituali, ita quod spiritualis Israel est quicumque fidelis, sanctorum Patriarcharum fidem ac mores amplectens, divina contemplans, adhærensque Christo, qui finis est legis ac Prophetarum.
paras.en: These expositions, however, are weakened by the fact that the Apostle, writing to the Romans, cites the text quoted above as foretelling the calling of the Gentiles. For thus says the holy Apostle: God [[Rom 9:22|endured with much patience vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction|sustinuit in multa patientia vasa iræ apta in interitum]], [[Rom 9:23|That he might shew the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy|ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ in vasa misericordiæ]]: [[Rom 9:24|whom also he hath called, not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles|Quos et vocavit, non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus]]. [[Rom 9:25|As in Osee he saith: I will call that which was not my people, my people|sicut in Osee dicit: Vocabo non plebem meam]]: [[Rom 9:25|and her that had not obtained mercy; one that hath obtained mercy|et non misericordiam consecutam, misericordiam consecutam]]. [[Rom 9:26|And it shalt be in the place where it was said unto them: you are not my people; there they shall be called the sons of the living God.|et erit in loco ubi dictum est eis, Non plebs mea vos; ibi vocabuntur filii Dei vivi]]. Following, then, the understanding of the divine Apostle, we must note that the Prophets and the Apostles were taught by the same Spirit and spoke by Him. Therefore, as in the New Testament a distinction is made among the Jews, or Israel, between carnal and spiritual (of the carnal the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:18|Behold Israel according to the flesh|Videte Israel secundum carnem]]; and John too in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 2:9|say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan|Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ]][[Apoc 3:9||]]; but of the spiritual Paul says: [[Gal 6:16|peace on them|Pax super eos]], [[Gal 6:16|and upon the Israel of God|et super Israel Dei]]), so the Prophets speak of a twofold Israel, namely carnal and spiritual, so that the spiritual Israel is every faithful man who embraces the faith and the ways of the holy Patriarchs, contemplates things divine, and cleaves to Christ, who is the end of the law and the Prophets.

paras.t: Est igitur sensus: Et erit numerus filiorum Israel, id est multitudo in Christum credentium, scilicet gentilium conversorum, Deum pura fide contemplantium, quasi arena maris, quia innumerabilis. Et erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos, id est ubique terrarum, ubi gentiles ante suam conversionem nominabantur, non filii Dei, sed dæmonum, quibus et serviebant (omnes enim dii gentium dæmonia), dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis, id est, ibi vocabuntur filii Dei, postquam ad Christum conversi exstiterint: sicut ad Galatas scribit Apostolus, Omnes filii Dei estis per fidem in Christo Jesu. Quotquot autem receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri.
paras.en: The sense, then, is this: [[1:10|And the number of the children of Israel|Et erit numerus filiorum Israel]], that is, the multitude of those who believe in Christ, namely of the converted Gentiles, who contemplate God with pure faith, [[1:10|as the sand of the sea|quasi arena maris]], for it is countless. [[1:10|And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people|Et erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos]]: that is, everywhere on earth, where the Gentiles before their conversion were called sons not of God but of the demons, whom they also served (for [[Ps 95:5|all the gods of the Gentiles are devils|omnes enim dii gentium dæmonia]]), [[1:10|it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis]]: that is, there they shall be called sons of God, once they have been converted to Christ; as the Apostle writes to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:26|you are all the children of God, by faith in Christ Jesus|Omnes filii Dei estis per fidem in Christo Jesu]]. [[John 1:12|But as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God|Quotquot autem receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri]].

paras.t: Et congregabuntur, congregatione spirituali per fidem et caritatem, vel etiam corporali, filii Juda, id est primitiva Ecclesia ex Judaismo conversa, puta Apostoli aliique credentes natione Judæi, et filii Israel pariter, constituendo unam Ecclesiam in Christo, tanquam in lapide angulari convenientes atque connexi. De quo subjungitur: Et ponent sibimet caput unum, id est, Christum unanimiter eligent in regem ac principem: quod non facerent, nisi electi prius essent ab ipso. Hinc scriptum est: Pax erit inter duos illos, videlicet gentiles et Judæos in Christum credentes. De hoc quoque capite Dominus testatur in Ezechiele: Ego pascam gregem meum, et ero eis in Deum, et servus meus David princeps eorum. Per David autem omnes intelligunt Christum, qui juxta Apostolum, est caput corporis Ecclesiæ. Quæ vero sequuntur, exponenda sunt sicut jam factum est.
paras.en: [[1:11|And|Et]] [[1:11|shall be gathered|congregabuntur]], with a spiritual gathering through faith and charity, or also a bodily one, [[1:11|the children of Juda|filii Juda]], that is, the primitive Church converted from Judaism, namely the Apostles and the other believers who were Jews by nation, [[1:11|and the children of Israel|et filii Israel]] [[1:11|together|pariter]], forming one Church in Christ, meeting and joined together in Him as in the corner stone. Of Him it is added: [[1:11|and they shall appoint themselves one head|Et ponent sibimet caput unum]]: that is, they shall with one mind choose Christ as their king and prince; which they would not do had they not first been chosen by Him. Hence it is written: [[Zach 6:13|the counsel of peace shall be between them both|Pax erit inter duos illos]] [Denis reads: "Peace shall be between those two"], namely the Gentiles and the Jews who believe in Christ. Of this head the Lord also testifies in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:15|I will feed my sheep|Ego pascam gregem meum]], [[Ezech 34:24|will be their God|et ero eis in Deum]], [[Ezech 34:24|and my servant David the prince|et servus meus David princeps]] of them. Now by David all understand Christ, who according to the Apostle is the head of the body, the Church[[Eph 5:23||]] [the margin gives Ephes. v, 23; Denis's words are those of Col 1:18]. What follows is to be expounded as has already been done.

1.title: EXPOSITIO MORALIS HUJUS PRIMI CAPITULI.
1.title_en: Moral exposition of this first chapter.

paras.t: Jam in superioribus dictum est, quod Osee (qui interpretatur Salvator) figura est Christi, de quo angelus ait : Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum; et Isaias, Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem. Per hoc ergo, quod Deus jussit Osee ut acciperet uxorem fornicationum, præfigurabatur quod Deus Pater dixit Christo, quando misit eum in mundum per incarnationis mysterium, ut acciperet uxorem fornicationum, id est, gentilitatem cum idolis fornicantem sibi desponsaret, atque ex ea exhiberet sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam. Unde et Christus loquitur: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere. In Isaia quoque Pater ait ad Christum : Parum est ut sis mihi ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas; dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. De hoc jam dicta sunt plura.
paras.en: It has been said above that Osee (which is interpreted *Saviour*) is a figure of Christ, of whom the angel says: [[Matt 1:21|he shall save his people from their sins|Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]; and Isaias: [[Is 45:8|let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem]]. By this, then, that God commanded Osee to take a wife of fornications, was prefigured what God the Father said to Christ when he sent him into the world through the mystery of the incarnation: that he should take [[1:2|a wife of fornications|uxorem fornicationum]], that is, that he should espouse to himself the Gentile world, which committed fornication with idols, and out of it [[Eph 5:27|present it to himself, a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle|exhiberet sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam]]. Hence Christ too says: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere]]. In Isaias, too, the Father says to Christ: [[Is 49:6|It is a small thing that thou shouldst be|Parum est ut sis mihi]] [[Is 49:6|to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to convert the dregs of Israel|ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas]]: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. Of this much has already been said.

paras.t: Porro quod Dominus ait de decem tribubus, Fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino, jam videmus in populo christiano, quomodo aliquorum deus venter est, quorum corda gravantur crapula et ebrietate. Alii avaritiæ (quod est idolorum servitus) student : qui dicunt auro, Robur meum; et obryzo, Fiducia mea : non metuentes quod ait Scriptura, Nihil est iniquius, quam amare pecuniam; et quod ait ad Timotheum Apostolum, Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli. Alii in sophismatibus ac vanitatibus suis jugiter occupantur. Contra quos clamat Joannes : Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris.
paras.en: Further, what the Lord says of the ten tribes, [[1:2|the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord|Fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino]], we now see in the Christian people: how for some [[Phil 3:19|God is their belly|deus venter est]], whose hearts are [[Luke 21:34|overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|gravantur crapula et ebrietate]]. Others are given to [[Col 3:5|covetousness, which is the service of idols|avaritiæ (quod est idolorum servitus)]]: who say to gold, My strength, and [[Job 31:24|to fine gold: My confidence|obryzo, Fiducia mea]]; not fearing what Scripture says, [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|Nihil est iniquius, quam amare pecuniam]]; and what the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli]]. Others are continually busied with their sophisms and vanities. Against whom John cries out: [[1 John 5:21|Little children, keep yourselves from idols|Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris]].

paras.t: Et abiit et accepit Gomer. Gomer interpretatur consummata sive perfecta. Per hoc itaque, quod Osee accepit Gomer, præsignatum est quod Christus accepit Ecclesiam ex gentibus congregatam, quæ ante conversionem suam fuerat consummata in vitiis, imo in fornicatione carnali et spirituali, eratque perfecta filia voluptatis. Postquam vero ad Christum conversa, et ei in sponsam unita est, facta est consummata in fide, spe et caritate; itemque perfecta in donis Spiritus Sancti, quemadmodum scribit Apostolus gentibus conversis, puta Corinthiis : Gratias ago Deo, quia in omnibus divites facti estis in illo, ita ut nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia. Hinc Salvator hortatur : Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est. Quumque Christus accepisset hanc sponsam, peperit ei filium, qui appellatus est Jezrael, id est, semen Dei. Ecclesia namque per verbum prædicationis et in fonte Baptismatis generat Christo filios gratiæ ac salutis, dicente Apostolo : Per Evangelium in Christo ego vos genui. Quod Ecclesia non faceret, nisi prius cognita atque fecundata esset a Christo, non semine materiali, sed luce cœlesti, donis ac virtute Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[1:3|So he went and took Gomer|Et abiit et accepit Gomer]]. Gomer is interpreted *consummate* or *perfect*. By this, then, that Osee took Gomer, it was foreshown that Christ took the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which before her conversion had been consummate in vices, nay, in carnal and spiritual fornication, and was a perfect daughter of pleasure. But after she was converted to Christ and joined to him as his bride, she was made consummate in faith, hope and charity, and likewise perfect in the gifts of the Holy Ghost; as the Apostle writes to converted Gentiles, namely the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 1:4|I give thanks|Gratias ago Deo]] to God that [[1 Cor 1:5|in all things you are made rich in him|in omnibus divites facti estis in illo]], [[1 Cor 1:7|So that nothing is wanting to you in any grace|ita ut nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia]]. Hence the Saviour exhorts: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]]. And when Christ had taken this bride, she [[1:3|bore him a son|peperit ei filium]], who was called [[1:4|Jezrahel|Jezrael]], that is, *seed of God*. For the Church, by the word of preaching and in the font of Baptism, begets to Christ sons of grace and salvation, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|Per Evangelium in Christo ego vos genui]]. And this the Church would not do unless she had first been known and made fruitful by Christ: not with material seed, but with heavenly light, with the gifts and power of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Insuper Dominus ait : Adhuc modicum, et visitabo sanguinem Jezrael : id est, occisionem seminis Dei, utpote Christi, et aliorum filiorum primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quos occiderunt Judæi, ulciscar, super domum Jehu, id est in populo Judæorum incredulo. Quod post quadraginta circiter annos a Christi passione impletum est, quando Romani destruxerunt Jerusalem ac Judæam, et Judæorum plurimos occiderunt, vendiderunt, disperserunt, et variis modis afflixerunt. Et in tempore illo contritus est arcus Israel, id est, tota fortitudo Judæorum est dejecta in valle Jezrael, id est in humilitate Christi et Ecclesiæ. Christus nempe sua humilitate ac passione promeruit sui ipsius exaltationem, judiciariam potestatem, adversariorum quoque suorum dejectionem. Idcirco superbi Judæi, Christum humilem persequendo, ejus humilitate dejecti sunt. Hieronymus et antiqui expositores, quorum temporibus abundabant hæretici, per decem tribus seu Israel, qui Dominum dereliquerunt, intelligunt hæreticos; per regnum vero seu populum Juda, Ecclesiam. Sicque per contritionem arcus Israel, designatur hæreticorum dejectio, qui Christi virtute vincuntur.
paras.en: Moreover the Lord says: [[1:4|yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezrahel|Adhuc modicum, et visitabo sanguinem Jezrael]]: that is, the slaying of the seed of God, namely of Christ and of the other sons of the primitive Church, whom the Jews slew, I will avenge [[1:4|upon the house of Jehu|super domum Jehu]], that is, on the unbelieving people of the Jews. This was fulfilled about forty years after the passion of Christ, when the Romans destroyed Jerusalem and Judea, and slew, sold, scattered and in various ways afflicted very many of the Jews. And at that time [[1:5|the bow of Israel|arcus Israel]] was broken, that is, the whole strength of the Jews was cast down, [[1:5|in the valley of Jezrahel|in valle Jezrael]], that is, in the humility of Christ and of the Church. For Christ by his humility and passion merited his own exaltation[[Phil 2:8||]][[Phil 2:9||]], judicial power, and also the casting down of his adversaries. Therefore the proud Jews, by persecuting the humble Christ, were cast down by his humility. Jerome and the ancient expositors, in whose times heretics abounded, understand by the ten tribes, or Israel, which forsook the Lord, the heretics, and by the kingdom or people of Juda, the Church. And so by the breaking of the bow of Israel is signified the casting down of the heretics, who are overcome by the power of Christ.

paras.t: Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filiam. Per hanc filiam Osee vel Gomer, quæ vocatur Absque misericordia, designantur hæretici, qui ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis deficiunt, dæmone suggerente, varios inducendo errores, et tanquam effeminati, tentationibus succumbendo. Hanc congregationem seu filiam, quæ divina misericordia meretur destitui, concepit a Christo Ecclesia, dum eos primo fideliter instruit atque baptizat; dum vero fidem rectam et ecclesiasticam deserunt unitatem, efficiuntur proles diaboli. De quibus ait in prima sua epistola Joannes : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis. Hinc Dominus ait : Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel, id est, conventiculis hæreticorum, qui æternaliter condemnantur ; sed domui Juda, id est, Ecclesiæ corde credenti et ore salubriter confitenti, miserebor, perducendo eos ad finem beatum.
paras.en: [[1:6|And she conceived again, and bore a daughter|Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filiam]]. By this daughter of Osee, or of Gomer, who is called [[1:6|Without mercy|Absque misericordia]], are signified the heretics, who [[Luke 8:13|believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis deficiunt]], at the devil's prompting, bringing in various errors and, as if effeminate, giving way to temptations. This congregation or daughter, which deserves to be deprived of the divine mercy, the Church conceived by Christ, when she first faithfully instructs and baptizes them; but when they forsake the right faith and the unity of the Church, they become the offspring of the devil. Of whom John says in his first epistle: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us|sed non erant ex nobis]]. Hence the Lord says: [[1:6|I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel|Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel]], that is, on the conventicles of the heretics, who are eternally condemned; but [[1:7|on the house of Juda|domui Juda]], that is, on the Church, which believes with the heart and confesses unto salvation with the mouth[[Rom 10:10||]], [[1:7|I will have mercy|miserebor]], bringing them to a blessed end.

paras.t: Et ablactavit eam quæ erat Absque misericordia, id est, præfatam hæreticorum collectionem privat Deus gratia internæ refectionis, lacte evangelicæ legis, pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris, quæ malevolam nequaquam ingreditur animam : ita ut tales non jam nutriantur in croceis, sed stercora amplexentur.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she weaned her that was called Without mercy|Et ablactavit eam quæ erat Absque misericordia]]: that is, God deprives the aforesaid gathering of heretics of the grace of inward refreshment, of the milk of the law of the Gospel, of [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|pane vitæ et intellectus]], and of [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aqua sapientiæ salutaris]], which by no means enters a malicious soul[[Wis 1:4||]]; so that such are no longer [[Lam 4:5|brought up in scarlet|nutriantur in croceis]], but embrace the dung.

paras.t: Et concepit et peperit filium. Et dixit : Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus. Per hunc tertium puerum Osee et Gomer, intelliguntur ceteri impii Christiani, qui rebelles sunt lumini, nec per gratiam et prædestinationem attinent Deo, sed sola fide Christiani filiique Ecclesiæ reputantur. De qualibus scriptum est : Ipsi de mundo sunt; et de mundo loquuntur, et mundus eos audit. De quibus ait Salvator : Multi dicent mihi in die illo : Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus, et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, et virtutes multas fecimus? et tunc confitebor illis : Quia nunquam novi vos ; discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis. Istis melius esset viam justitiæ ignorasse, quam cognitam abjecisse : in quibus utique semen Dei non permanet. Horum Deus omnium asserit se non esse Deum, quia nec ipsi eum super omnia amant et colunt, nec ipse per gratiam corda eorum inhabitat, neque per providentiam singularem providet eis efficienter de necessariis ad salutem ; verum dimittit eos, justitia exigente, secundum desideria cordis eorum, ut eant in adinventionibus suis. Quocontra de electis habetur in Apocalypsi : Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eorum Deus.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she conceived, and bore a son|Et concepit et peperit filium]]. [[1:9|And he said: Call his name, Not my people|Et dixit : Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus]]. By this third child of Osee and Gomer are understood the rest of the wicked Christians, who are rebels to the light, and do not belong to God by grace and predestination, but are reckoned Christians and sons of the Church by faith alone. Of such it is written: [[1 John 4:5|They are of the world. Therefore of the world they speak: and the world heareth them|Ipsi de mundo sunt; et de mundo loquuntur, et mundus eos audit]]. Of whom the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:22|Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord, have not we prophesied in thy name, and cast out devils in thy name, and done many miracles|Multi dicent mihi in die illo : Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus, et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, et virtutes multas fecimus?]]? [[Matt 7:23|And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you|et tunc confitebor illis : Quia nunquam novi vos]]; [[Luke 13:27|depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity|discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis]] [the margin gives Matt. vii, 22, 23; the last clause is in the words of Luke 13:27, where Matthew has *you that work iniquity*]. For these it would have been better not to have known the way of justice than to have cast it away once known[[2 Pet 2:21||]]: in them the seed of God surely does not remain. Of all these God declares that he is not their God, because neither do they love and worship him above all things, nor does he dwell in their hearts by grace, nor provide them effectually, by a special providence, with what is necessary for salvation; but he lets them go, as justice requires, [[Ps 80:13|according to the desires of their heart|secundum desideria cordis eorum]], that they may walk [[Ps 80:13|in their own inventions|in adinventionibus suis]]. Whereas of the elect it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and God himself with them shall be their God|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eorum Deus]].

2.title: DECLARATIO SECUNDI CAPITULI : DICITE FRATRIBUS VESTRIS : POPULUS MEUS.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: Say ye to your brethren: My people.

paras.t: NUNC in fine præcedentis capituli dictum est, quemadmodum filii Juda et filii Israel congregarentur, et constituerent sibi caput unum, concorditer credendo in Christum. Apostolica quoque auctoritate ostensum est, quod per filios Israel, intelligantur spirituales Israelitæ, id est electi gentiles, juxta illud ad Galatas : Qui ex fide sunt, hi sunt filii Abrahæ. Idcirco Propheta alloquitur modo prædicatores primitivæ Ecclesiæ natione Judæos, puta Apostolos aliosque Christi discipulos, ut gentilibus gratiam Dei annuntient.
paras.en: AT the end of the preceding chapter it was said how the children of Juda and the children of Israel should be gathered together and appoint themselves one head, believing with one accord in Christ. It was also shown on the Apostle's authority that by the children of Israel are understood the spiritual Israelites, that is, the chosen Gentiles, according to that saying to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:7|they who are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham|Qui ex fide sunt, hi sunt filii Abrahæ]]. Therefore the Prophet now addresses the preachers of the primitive Church who were Jews by nation, namely the Apostles and the other disciples of Christ, that they may announce the grace of God to the Gentiles.

paras.t: Dicite, o Apostoli et ex Judaismo conversi, fratribus vestris, id est electis ex gentibus : qui sunt fratres vestri, non solum propter conformitatem naturæ et ratione originis ex primo parente, itemque quoniam ab eodem geniti Creatore (secundum illud Malachiæ : Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum ? Numquid non Deus unus creavit nos?), sed etiam propter conformitatem fidei, caritatis et gratiæ. Unde ad Galatas testatur Apostolus : In Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet, neque præputium, sed fides quæ per dilectionem operatur. De talibus fratribus Dominus ait electis Judæis per Isaiam : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes, in Africam et Lydiam, in Græciam et Italiam ; et adducent omnes fratres vestros. Itaque, Dicite fratribus vestris : Populus meus, id est, quod ipsi per gratiam sunt populus meus, sicut et vos. Propter quod ad Romanos dicit Apostolus : An Judæorum Deus tantum ? Nonne et gentium ? Rursusque : Non est distinctio Judæi et Græci; nam idem Dominus omnium, dives in omnes qui invocant eum. Hinc per Isaiam loquitur Dominus : Dicam Ægypto, Populus meus; et opus manuum mearum, Assyrio. Et sorori vestræ, id est Ecclesiæ ex gentibus congregatæ, dicite : Misericordiam consecuta, id est, quod ipsa misericordiam meam suscepit per gratiam Christi. Propter quod in Isaia habetur : Ecce gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis. Et in Actibus ait Petrus : Si Deus eamdem gratiam dedit illis (videlicet gentibus) sicut et nobis, ego quis eram, qui possem prohibere Deum ? Hoc est quod ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus : Revelatum est sanctis Apostolis et Prophetis in Spiritu, esse gentes coheredes et concorporales, et comparticipes promissionis Dei in Christo Jesu.
paras.en: [[2:1|Say ye|Dicite]], O Apostles and you converted from Judaism, [[2:1|to your brethren|fratribus vestris]], that is, to the elect from among the Gentiles: who are your brethren not only by likeness of nature and by reason of their origin from the first parent, and also because they were brought into being by the same Creator (according to that saying of Malachias: [[Mal 2:10|Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?|Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum ? Numquid non Deus unus creavit nos?]]), but also by likeness of faith, charity and grace. Whence the Apostle testifies to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:6|in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing nor uncircumcision: but faith that worketh by Charity|In Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet, neque præputium, sed fides quæ per dilectionem operatur]]. Of such brethren the Lord says to the elect Jews through Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes]], [[Is 66:19|into Africa, and Lydia|in Africam et Lydiam]], into Greece and Italy; [[Is 66:20|and they shall bring all your brethren|et adducent omnes fratres vestros]]. So then, [[2:1|Say ye to your brethren: You are my people|Dicite fratribus vestris : Populus meus]], that is, that they through grace are my people, as you are also. For which reason the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 3:29|Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles?|An Judæorum Deus tantum ? Nonne et gentium ?]] And again: [[Rom 10:12|there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek: for the same is Lord over all, rich unto all that call upon him|Non est distinctio Judæi et Græci; nam idem Dominus omnium, dives in omnes qui invocant eum]]. Hence the Lord speaks through Isaias: I will say to Egypt and to the Assyrian: [[Is 19:25|my people of Egypt, and the work of my hands to the Assyrian|Populus meus; et opus manuum mearum, Assyrio]] [Denis's wording: ‘I will say to Egypt, My people; and to the Assyrian, The work of my hands’]. [[2:1|and to your sister|Et sorori vestræ]], that is, to the Church gathered from the Gentiles, say: [[2:1|Thou hast obtained mercy|Misericordiam consecuta]], that is, that she has received my mercy through the grace of Christ. For which reason it is found in Isaias: [[Is 55:5|Behold thou shalt call a nation, which thou knewest not|Ecce gentem quam nesciebas, vocabis]]. And in the Acts Peter says: [[Acts 11:17|If then God gave them the same grace|Si Deus eamdem gratiam dedit illis]] (namely to the Gentiles) [[Acts 11:17|as to us also|sicut et nobis]], [[Acts 11:17|who was I, that could withstand God?|ego quis eram, qui possem prohibere Deum ?]] This is what the Apostle says to the Ephesians: [[Eph 3:5|revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit|Revelatum est sanctis Apostolis et Prophetis in Spiritu]], [[Eph 3:6|That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs and of the same body: and copartners of his promise in Christ Jesus|esse gentes coheredes et concorporales, et comparticipes promissionis Dei in Christo Jesu]].

paras.t: Præterea, præter hanc expositionem tangit Hieronymus alias duas. Prima est : Dicite, o vos de tribu et populo Juda, unum Deum colentes, fratribus vestris, id est populo decem tribuum, quod sit populus meus, dummodo voluerint idololatriam et alia peccata abjicere. Et quia de semine Patriarcharum progenitus est, et sorori vestræ, id est eidem plebi vel Synagogæ, dicite quod sit misericordiam consecuta. Nam multi ex decem tribubus gratiose salvati sunt, quorum unus fuit Tobias de tribu Nephthali. — Secunda est : Vos, Judæi qui creditis, dicite fratribus vestris, id est fractis ramis, quod sit populus meus, et sorori vestræ Synagogæ, quod sit misericordiam consecuta, quoad hoc quod in fine mundi, quum intraverit plenitudo gentium, omnis Israel salvus erit.
paras.en: Besides this exposition, Jerome touches on two others. The first is: [[2:1|Say ye|Dicite]], O you of the tribe and people of Juda who worship the one God, [[2:1|to your brethren|fratribus vestris]], that is, to the people of the ten tribes, that it is [[2:1|my people|populus meus]], provided they are willing to cast away idolatry and their other sins. And since it was begotten of the seed of the Patriarchs, [[2:1|and to your sister|et sorori vestræ]], that is, to the same people or Synagogue, say: [[2:1|Thou hast obtained mercy|misericordiam consecuta]]. For many of the ten tribes were saved by grace, one of whom was Tobias of the tribe of Nephthali. — The second is: You Jews who believe, say [[2:1|to your brethren|fratribus vestris]], that is, to the broken branches, that it is my people, and to your sister the Synagogue, that she has obtained mercy, in this respect: that at the end of the world, when [[Rom 11:25|the fulness of the Gentiles|plenitudo gentium]] shall have come in, [[Rom 11:26|all Israel should be saved|omnis Israel salvus erit]].

paras.t: Judicate matrem vestram, judicate : quoniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus. Hunc locum Beda exponit pro tempore Christi, ut sit sensus : O Apostoli et ceteri credentes ex Judaismo, judicate, id est reprehendite, matrem vestram incredulam Synagogam Christo. Et repetit, judicate, quatenus frequenter ac strenue increpent eam. Quod in Actibus leguntur fecisse Apostoli, dicente Petro Judæis : Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem vos quidem tradidistis, et negastis ante faciem Pilati, et petistis virum homicidam donari vobis. Quia ipsa Synagoga incredula, non est uxor mea, quum non sit mihi per fidem et caritatem conjuncta, non imprægnetur a me fructu operum bonorum ; et ego non sum vir ejus, id est sponsus, ita, quia non est æterna conjunctio spiritualis matrimonii inter eam et me, quoniam peccata ejus diviserunt inter eam et me, et facta est meretrix atque adultera : sicut patebit. Loquitur autem Deus de spirituali conjunctione, quæ est inter creaturam rationalem et Creatorem, metaphorice sub nomine uxoris et viri. Et simili modo ait per Isaiam : Quis est iste libellus repudii, quo dimisi matrem vestram? Ei quoque quod nunc Dominus ait, Judicate matrem vestram, simile est quod per eumdem Isaiam Dominus ait : Et nunc, habitatores Jerusalem, et viri Juda, judicate inter me et vineam meam, videlicet Synagogam.
paras.en: [[2:2|Judge your mother, judge her: because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband|Judicate matrem vestram, judicate : quoniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus]]. Bede expounds this place of the time of Christ, so that the sense is: O Apostles and the rest of the believers from Judaism, [[2:2|judge|judicate]], that is, rebuke, [[2:2|your mother|matrem vestram]], the Synagogue that does not believe in Christ. And he repeats [[2:2|judge her|judicate]], so that they may rebuke her often and vigorously. This we read in the Acts that the Apostles did, when Peter said to the Jews: [[Acts 3:13|the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus, whom you indeed delivered up and denied before the face of Pilate|Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem vos quidem tradidistis, et negastis ante faciem Pilati]], [[Acts 3:14|and desired a murderer to be granted unto you|et petistis virum homicidam donari vobis]]. [[2:2|because she|Quia ipsa]], the unbelieving Synagogue, [[2:2|is not my wife|non est uxor mea]], since she is not joined to me by faith and charity, and is not made fruitful by me with the fruit of good works; [[2:2|and I am not her husband|et ego non sum vir ejus]], that is, her bridegroom, in this way: because there is no everlasting union of spiritual marriage between her and me, since her sins [[Is 59:2|have divided between|diviserunt inter]] her and me, and she has become a harlot and an adulteress, as will appear. Now God speaks of the spiritual union which there is between the rational creature and the Creator, metaphorically under the name of wife and husband. And in like manner he says through Isaias: [[Is 50:1|What is this bill of the divorce of your mother, with which I have put her away?|Quis est iste libellus repudii, quo dimisi matrem vestram?]] [the margin gives Ibid. i, 1, that is Is 50:1]. With what the Lord now says, [[2:2|Judge your mother|Judicate matrem vestram]], there agrees also what the Lord says through the same Isaias: [[Is 5:3|And now, O ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and ye men of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard|Et nunc, habitatores Jerusalem, et viri Juda, judicate inter me et vineam meam]], namely the Synagogue.

paras.t: Consequenter Deus clementer hortatur Synagogam ad pœnitentiam, et ut illa magis obediat admonitioni divinæ, minatur pœnam. Auferat, id est, relinquat atque abjiciat, fornicationes suas spirituales, id est idolorum culturas ; fornicationes quoque corporales, id est illicitos concubitus soluti cum soluta ; a facie sua, id est ab adspectu atque præsentia sua, ne eas per approbationem adspiciat vel acceptet, sed retro se jactet : quemadmodum per Jeremiam Dominus asserit, Si abstuleris offendicula tua a facie mea, non commoveberis. Nihilo minus debet homo peccata sua ante se ponere, ut ea pœnitendo penset ac defleat, dicente Psalmista : Quoniam iniquitatem meam ego cognosco. Propter quod Dominus ait per Jeremiam : Leva oculos tuos in directum, et vide ubi non prostrata sis. Et adulteria sua spiritualia ac corporalia auferat de medio uberum suorum, id est a suis uberibus, vel a corde, quod intra ubera situatur. Corporalia quippe adulteria per contactum uberum provocantur, et consummantur : idcirco de uberibus tolli jubentur. Spiritualia vero adulteria per cordis delectationem explentur. Præcipitur ergo, ne cor vitia idololatriæ diligat, nec ea ad actum deducat. Quamvis autem spiritualis fornicatio præsertim idololatria appelletur, quia per eam cor a Deo formaliter atque totaliter separatur; quodlibet tamen peccatum mortale, fornicatio spiritualis est, quia per ipsum mens, cœlestis Sponsi unione relicta, summique boni adhæsione rejecta, rebus inhæret caducis, et in creaturis potius quam in Deo quiescit ac delectatur. Propter quod in Numeris Dominus : Ne sequantur (inquit) cogitationes suas, et oculos per res varias fornicantes ; et in Ezechiele, Contrivi cor eorum fornicans, et recedens a me.
paras.en: Next God mercifully exhorts the Synagogue to penance, and so that she may the more obey the divine admonition, he threatens punishment. [[2:2|Let her put away|Auferat]], that is, let her leave and cast off, [[2:2|her fornications|fornicationes suas]], the spiritual ones, that is, the worship of idols, and the bodily ones too, that is, the unlawful lying together of an unmarried man with an unmarried woman; [[2:2|from her face|a facie sua]], that is, from her sight and presence, so that she may not look upon them with approval or accept them, but cast them behind her: as the Lord declares through Jeremias: [[Jer 4:1|if thou wilt take away thy stumblingblocks out of my sight, thou shalt not be moved|Si abstuleris offendicula tua a facie mea, non commoveberis]]. None the less a man ought to set his sins before him, so as to weigh them and bewail them in penance, as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 50:5|For I know my iniquity|Quoniam iniquitatem meam ego cognosco]] [the margin reads Ps. i, 5, a misreading of l, 5]. For which reason the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:2|Lift up thy eyes on high: and see where thou hast not prostituted thyself|Leva oculos tuos in directum, et vide ubi non prostrata sis]]. [[2:2|and her adulteries|Et adulteria sua]], spiritual and bodily, let her put away [[2:2|from between her breasts|de medio uberum suorum]], that is, from her breasts, or from the heart, which is placed between the breasts. For bodily adulteries are provoked and consummated by touching of the breasts: therefore they are commanded to be taken away from the breasts. But spiritual adulteries are fulfilled by the delight of the heart. It is therefore commanded that the heart should not love the vices of idolatry, nor carry them out in act. Now although idolatry especially is called spiritual fornication, because by it the heart is formally and wholly separated from God, yet every mortal sin is a spiritual fornication, because by it the mind, leaving its union with the heavenly Bridegroom and casting off its cleaving to the highest good, cleaves to perishable things, and rests and delights in creatures rather than in God. For which reason the Lord says in Numbers: Let them [[Num 15:39|not follow|Ne sequantur]], he says, [[Num 15:39|their own thoughts and eyes going astray after divers things|cogitationes suas, et oculos per res varias fornicantes]] [*fornicantes*, literally ‘going a-whoring’]; and in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 6:9|I have broken their heart that was faithless, and revolted from me|Contrivi cor eorum fornicans, et recedens a me]] [*fornicans*, ‘that went a-whoring’, where the Douay-Rheims has ‘faithless’].

paras.t: Ne forte exspoliem, id est, exspoliando faciam, eam nudam, id est spiritualibus gratiis vel corporalibus beneficiis destitutam. Vestes nempe et ornamenta populi Israel, fuerunt auxilium Dei, angelorum custodia, doctrina legis et Prophetarum, religiosæ ac sanctæ personæ, et cetera dona Creatoris, de quibus gloriabantur, dicentes : Non fecit taliter omni nationi, et judicia sua non manifestavit eis. Hæc Deus minatur se ablaturum, nisi pœniteant. Et statuam, id est ponam, eam secundum diem nativitatis suæ, id est in tali ac tanta calamitate, vilitate et abjectione, qualem et quantam habuit in Ægypto, ubi multiplicatus est populus Israel, et multis ærumnis, idololatriis, atque durissimo jugo fuit subjectus. Propter quod in Ezechiele scriptum est : In die ortus tui non est præcisus umbilicus tuus, et aqua non es lota, sed projecta super faciem terræ. Et denuo : In die, inquit, qua nata es, non es sale salita ; et transivi per te, et inveni te nudam et deturpatam, et conspersam in sanguine tuo. Sed de tanta ærumna eripuit Deus hanc plebem, quum eam eduxerat de Ægypto. Propter quod subdit : Indui te bysso et subtilibus, et ornamenta circumposui tibi. Hæc autem vidimus jam Judæis ablata propter incredulitatem suam in Christum.
paras.en: [[2:3|Lest I strip her|Ne forte exspoliem]], that is, by stripping make her, [[2:3|naked|eam nudam]], that is, bereft of spiritual graces or bodily benefits. For the garments and ornaments of the people of Israel were the help of God, the guard of the angels, the teaching of the Law and the Prophets, religious and holy persons, and the other gifts of the Creator, in which they gloried, saying: [[Ps 147:9|He hath not done in like manner to every nation: and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them|Non fecit taliter omni nationi, et judicia sua non manifestavit eis]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 20, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 147:9]. These things God threatens to take away unless they repent. [[2:3|and set her|Et statuam]], that is, place her, [[2:3|as in the day that she was born|secundum diem nativitatis suæ]], that is, in such and so great calamity, vileness and abjection as she had in Egypt, where the people of Israel was multiplied, and was subjected to many hardships, to idolatries, and to a most hard yoke. For which reason it is written in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:4|in the day of thy nativity thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed with water|In die ortus tui non est præcisus umbilicus tuus, et aqua non es lota]], [[Ezech 16:5|but thou wast cast out upon the face of the earth|sed projecta super faciem terræ]]. And again: [[Ezech 16:5|in the day|In die]], he says, [[Ezech 16:5|that thou wast born|qua nata es]], thou wast not [[Ezech 16:4|salted with salt|sale salita]]; and I passed by thee, and found thee naked and disfigured, and sprinkled with thy blood[[Ezech 16:6||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xvi, 4–8; Denis recalls vv. 6–7 loosely]. But from such great hardship God rescued this people when he had brought it out of Egypt. For which reason he adds: I clothed thee with fine linen and fine garments[[Ezech 16:10||]], and set ornaments about thee[[Ezech 16:11||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xvi, 10–13]. These things we have now seen taken away from the Jews because of their unbelief in Christ.

paras.t: Et ponam eam quasi solitudinem, id est, habitatores terræ eorum occidam, vel transferam de propria terra. Unde Christus in Evangelio ait Judæis : Relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta. Et statuam eam velut terram inviam, id est, Synagogam parificabo terræ quæ viam non habet, eo quod non sit habitator vel deambulator in ea. Sic Synagoga a Deo derelicta est, nec habet rectam viam tendendi ad Deum, quemadmodum Isaias testatur : Fuisti derelicta et odio habita, et non erat qui per te transiret. Et interficiam eam siti. Hoc accipi potest de siti corporali, quam Judæi perpessi sunt, a Romanis obsessi ; tunc enim defuerunt eis cibi ac potus : vel de siti spirituali, id est aviditate audiendi verbum Dei. Nunc enim Judæi multo tempore desiderarunt habere et audire Prophetam, qui eis aliquid certi de Messiæ nuntiaret adventu, dolentesque dicunt : Signa nostra non vidimus, jam non est Propheta. Sed exigentibus culpis suis, non merentur divinitus exaudiri. De hujusmodi fame et siti Dominus ait per Amos : Emittam famem in terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei. Interficiuntur quoque obstinati Judæi siti, id est penuria aquæ sapientiæ salutaris gratiæque cœlestis. De qua dicit Salvator : Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum ; sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Occiduntur quoque siti, id est immoderato temporalium rerum affectu, quum sint avarissimi.
paras.en: [[2:3|and I will make her as a wilderness|Et ponam eam quasi solitudinem]], that is, I will slay the inhabitants of their land, or carry them away from their own land. Whence Christ says to the Jews in the Gospel: [[Matt 23:38|your house shall be left to you, desolate|Relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta]]. [[2:3|and will set her as a land that none can pass through|Et statuam eam velut terram inviam]], that is, I will make the Synagogue like a land that has no road, because there is no one living or walking in it. So the Synagogue has been forsaken by God, and has no straight way of going to God, as Isaias testifies: [[Is 60:15|thou wast forsaken, and hated, and there was none that passed through thee|Fuisti derelicta et odio habita, et non erat qui per te transiret]]. [[2:3|and will kill her with drought|Et interficiam eam siti]] [*sitis*, ‘thirst’]. This can be taken of bodily thirst, which the Jews suffered when besieged by the Romans, for then food and drink failed them; or of spiritual thirst, that is, eagerness to hear the word of God. For now for a long time the Jews have desired to have and to hear a Prophet who might tell them something certain of the coming of the Messias, and they say in sorrow: [[Ps 73:9|Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet|Signa nostra non vidimus, jam non est Propheta]]. But as their sins demand, they do not deserve to be heard by God. Of hunger and thirst of this kind the Lord says through Amos: [[Amos 8:11|I will send forth a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord|Emittam famem in terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei]]. The obstinate Jews are also slain by thirst, that is, by want of the water of saving wisdom and of heavenly grace; of which the Saviour says: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum]]; [[John 4:14|But the water that I will give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]. They are slain also by thirst, that is, by an immoderate desire for temporal things, since they are most avaricious.

paras.t: Præterea, quidam omnia jam prædicta, ab illo loco, Judicate matrem vestram, exponunt de Judæis pro tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis, ita quod Propheta alloquitur Prophetas et justos, qui captivitatem illam prædixerunt, videlicet Jeremiam, Baruch, quatenus Jerusalem vel Synagogam judicent, atque ex ejus pravitate perpendant quod non sit sponsa seu uxor Dei, nec ipse sit sponsus virque ipsius. Cetera quoque quæ dicta sunt, applicari possunt Judæis temporis illius, eodem sensu quo nunc applicata sunt Judæis pro tempore Christi. Multum enim viguit utraque fornicatio præinducta in populo Judæorum ante Babylonicam captivitatem. Propter quod Deus per manum Chaldæorum eos exspoliavit, et velut solitudinem terramque inviam statuit, prout per Jeremiam prædixit ubertim. Unde loco quodam loquitur Dominus : Derelinquam vos et civitatem quam dedi vobis et patribus vestris ; et dabo vos in vexationem et maledictionem, et in stuporem, et in sibilum, et in opprobrium, eo quod non audieritis verba mea. Denique sicut prædicta, sic et sequentia utroque modo exponuntur, et sensus redit in idem.
paras.en: Furthermore, some expound everything said so far, from the place [[2:2|Judge your mother|Judicate matrem vestram]], of the Jews at the time of the Babylonian captivity, so that the Prophet is addressing the Prophets and just men who foretold that captivity, namely Jeremias and Baruch, that they should judge Jerusalem or the Synagogue, and weigh from her depravity that she is not the bride or wife of God, nor he her bridegroom and husband. The rest of what has been said can also be applied to the Jews of that time, in the same sense in which it has now been applied to the Jews of the time of Christ. For both kinds of fornication spoken of above flourished greatly among the Jewish people before the Babylonian captivity. For which reason God stripped them by the hand of the Chaldeans, and set them as a wilderness and a land that none can pass through, as he foretold abundantly through Jeremias. Whence in one place the Lord says: I [[Jer 23:39|will forsake you, and the city which I gave to you, and to your fathers|Derelinquam vos et civitatem quam dedi vobis et patribus vestris]]; and I will give you up to vexation[[Jer 24:9||]] and a curse, and to astonishment and a hissing[[Jer 25:18||]], and to reproach[[Jer 23:40||]], because [[Jer 25:8|you have not heard my words|non audieritis verba mea]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiii, 39, 40; xxiv, 9; xxv, 18, 8: Denis joins phrases from these verses]. Finally, as what has gone before, so also what follows is expounded in both ways, and the sense comes back to the same.

paras.t: Et filiorum illius, id est filiorum infidelis Synagogæ, sequentium matris suæ perfidiam et peccata : quibus in Evangelio dicitur, Genimina viperarum, quomodo fugietis a judicio gehennæ? non miserebor : quoniam a Chaldæis ac Romanis vastati sunt; et bona gratiæ in præsenti, bonaque gloriæ in futuro perdiderunt. Unde Dominus ait ad Jeremiam : Non assumas laudem et orationem pro eis; si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum. Quoniam filii fornicationum sunt, id est, multiformium fornicationum vitiis servierunt. Propter quod filii fornicationum vocantur, propter abundantiam hujusmodi vitii, sicut Antichristus dicitur homo peccati et filius perditionis. Vel dicuntur filii fornicationum, quia a parentibus fornicatoribus nati non solum in esse naturæ, sed etiam culpæ, quoniam patres docuerunt filios suos errores et scelera.
paras.en: And [[2:4|on her children|Et filiorum illius]], that is, on the children of the unbelieving Synagogue, who follow their mother's faithlessness and sins, to whom it is said in the Gospel: [[Matt 23:33|generation of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of hell?|Genimina viperarum, quomodo fugietis a judicio gehennæ?]], [[2:4|I will not have mercy|non miserebor]]: for they were laid waste by the Chaldeans and the Romans, and lost the goods of grace in the present and the goods of glory in the future. Whence the Lord says to Jeremias: [[Jer 7:16|nor take to thee praise and supplication for them|Non assumas laudem et orationem pro eis]]; [[Jer 15:1|If Moses and Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not towards this people|si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum]]. [[2:4|for they are the children of fornications|Quoniam filii fornicationum sunt]], that is, they have served the vices of fornications of many kinds. For this reason they are called children of fornications, because of the abundance of this vice, as Antichrist is called [[2 Thess 2:3|the man of sin|homo peccati]] and [[2 Thess 2:3|the son of perdition|filius perditionis]]. Or they are called children of fornications because they were born of fornicating parents, not only in the being of nature but also in that of guilt, since the fathers taught their children errors and crimes.

paras.t: Quia fornicata est mater eorum, videlicet Synagoga, ut patuit. Unde Jeremias, Unusquisque, ait, ad uxorem proximi sui hinniebat. Et repleta fuit idolis terra eorum, ut Isaias dixit. Confusa est incredula Synagoga, id est, obstupuit, admirata est, estque vitiis inordinata, et confusione digna effecta, quæ concepit eos, id est filios fornicationum prædictos, quos enutrivit diabolo, instruens eos in malo. Sed obviare videtur illud Jeremiæ : Confusione non sunt confusi, et erubescere noluerunt. Et respondendum, quod sicut in Ecclesiastico habetur, Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gratiam et gloriam. Confusio itaque una est mala, peccati inductiva, dum quis præ rubore abscondit vitia sua. Alia vero est bona, dum homo erubescit de malo culpæ. De hac secunda loquitur Jeremias. Sic enim obstinati non confunduntur, nec verecundantur impie operari. Propter quod obstinatæ plebi Judæorum dicitur a Jeremia : Frons meretricis mulieris facta est tibi, noluisti erubescere. De talibus loquitur Isaias : Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt; et Salomon, Lætantur quum malefecerint. Præter hanc duplicem confusionem est confusio tertia, dum aliquis frustratur spe sua, et adversariorum suorum voluntati exponitur, atque ignominiosam incidit calamitatem. De qua orat Psalmista : Deus meus, in te confido, non erubescam; neque irrideant me inimici mei. De hac quoque loquitur nunc Osee. Subditur enim ratio hujusmodi confusionis :
paras.en: [[2:5|For their mother hath committed fornication|Quia fornicata est mater eorum]], namely the Synagogue, as has been shown. Whence Jeremias: [[Jer 5:8|every one|Unusquisque]], he says, [[Jer 5:8|neighed after his neighbour's wife|ad uxorem proximi sui hinniebat]]. And their land was filled with idols[[Is 2:8||]], as Isaias said. [[2:5|is covered with shame|Confusa est]] [*confusa est*, ‘is confounded’, on which the discussion of *confusio*, shame or confusion, below turns] the unbelieving Synagogue, that is, she was stunned and amazed, and is disordered by vices and made worthy of confusion, [[2:5|she that conceived them|quæ concepit eos]], that is, the children of fornications just spoken of, whom she reared for the devil, instructing them in evil. But that saying of Jeremias seems to stand against this: [[Jer 6:15|they were not confounded with confusion, and they knew not how to blush|Confusione non sunt confusi, et erubescere noluerunt]] [Denis: *noluerunt*, ‘would not’]. And the answer must be that, as is found in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 4:25|there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame that bringeth glory and grace|Est confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gratiam et gloriam]]. So one confusion is bad, leading to sin, when someone out of blushing hides his vices. But the other is good, when a man blushes for the evil of guilt. Of this second Jeremias speaks; for so the obstinate are not confounded, nor ashamed to act wickedly. For which reason it is said by Jeremias to the obstinate people of the Jews: [[Jer 3:3|thou hadst a harlot's forehead, thou wouldst not blush|Frons meretricis mulieris facta est tibi, noluisti erubescere]]. Of such Isaias speaks: [[Is 3:9|they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom, and they have not hid it|Peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt]]; and Solomon: [[Prov 2:14|are glad when they have done evil|Lætantur quum malefecerint]]. Besides this twofold confusion there is a third, when someone is cheated of his hope, and is exposed to the will of his adversaries, and falls into a shameful calamity. Of this the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 24:2|In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed|Deus meus, in te confido, non erubescam]]; [[Ps 24:3|Neither let my enemies laugh at me|neque irrideant me inimici mei]]. Of this too Osee now speaks; for the reason for such confusion is added:

paras.t: Quia dixit mater serpentina ac infidelis : Vadam, spiritualiter per fidem, vel potius infidelitatem et cultum, post amatores meos, id est deos quos colui, vel homines in quibus magis quam in Deo vero confisa sum, id est, idolis adhærebo, vel hominum quæram subsidia. Hoc dixerunt Judæi ex diffidentia divini auxilii. Quemadmodum enim in Jeremia copiose describitur, quum sanctus Jeremias hortaretur eos ad idololatriæ rejectionem, dixerunt : Non audiemus verbum ex te, sed facientes faciemus omne verbum quod egreditur ex ore nostro, ut sacrificemus reginæ cœli. Qui dant panes mihi, et aquas meas, et lanam meam, et linum meum, et oleum meum, et potum, id est necessaria victui atque vestitui. Hæc enim arbitrabantur sibi conferri ab idolis, vel mundanis hominibus potius quam a Deo. Spiritualiter dedit Deus electis Judæis panem vitæ et intellectus, aquas quoque sapientiæ salutaris, de quibus loquitur Isaias, Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris; lanam etiam et linum, id est indumenta seu decorem virtutum, de quibus Isaias inducit, Induit me vestimento salutis, et indumento justitiæ circumdedit me; itemque oleum unctionis et consolationis internæ, et potum spiritualiter inebriantem, ab æstu concupiscentiæ refrigerantem, ipsamque animam in Deo lætificantem. Unde et scriptum est : Torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos. Potus iste est fervor divini amoris, seu exuberantia gratiæ deiformis : per quem cuncta terrena desipiunt, solaque sapiunt bona æterna.
paras.en: [[2:5|for she said|Quia dixit]], the serpentine and unbelieving mother: [[2:5|I will go|Vadam]], spiritually, by faith, or rather by unbelief, and by worship, [[2:5|after my lovers|post amatores meos]], that is, the gods whom I have worshipped, or the men in whom I have trusted more than in the true God; that is, I will cleave to idols, or seek the help of men. This the Jews said out of distrust of the divine help. For as is described at length in Jeremias, when holy Jeremias was exhorting them to cast away idolatry, they said: [[Jer 44:16|we will not hearken to thee|Non audiemus verbum ex te]]: [[Jer 44:17|But we will certainly do every word that shall proceed out of our own mouth, to sacrifice to the queen of heaven|sed facientes faciemus omne verbum quod egreditur ex ore nostro, ut sacrificemus reginæ cœli]]. [[2:5|that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, my oil, and my drink|Qui dant panes mihi, et aquas meas, et lanam meam, et linum meum, et oleum meum, et potum]], that is, what is needed for food and clothing. For they supposed that these things were bestowed on them by idols, or by worldly men, rather than by God. Spiritually, God gave the elect Jews [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|panem vitæ et intellectus]], and also [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aquas quoque sapientiæ salutaris]], of which Isaias speaks: [[Is 12:3|Thou shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour's fountains:|Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris]]; wool also and flax, that is, the clothing or beauty of the virtues, of which Isaias brings in: [[Is 61:10|he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation: and with the robe of justice he hath covered me|Induit me vestimento salutis, et indumento justitiæ circumdedit me]]; and likewise the oil of anointing and of inward consolation, and a drink that spiritually inebriates, cools from the heat of concupiscence, and gladdens the soul itself in God. Whence also it is written: [[Ps 35:9|thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure|Torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos]]. That drink is the fervour of divine love, or the overflowing of deiform grace, by which all earthly things lose their savour, and only the eternal goods have savour [the Latin plays on *desipiunt* and *sapiunt*].

paras.t: Propter hoc, id est, quia dixisti, Vadam post amatores meos, ecce ego Dominus sepiam, id est, vallabo et implicabo, viam tuam, id est desiderium vel actionem qua nitebaris ire ad amatores nocivos, spinis, id est doloribus et ærumnis adversitatibusque diversis, et sepiam eam maceria, id est muro seu grandi obstaculo, quo impedietur venire quo ivit. Et semitas suas non inveniet, id est, affectum suum non poterit perducere ad effectum. Non enim permisit Deus Judæos hos adipisci optata auxilia a diis vel hominibus in quibus sperabant; sed gravissimis pœnis eos addixit, per obsidionem Chaldæorum ac Romanorum, ita quod nullus potuit eis opem impendere. Insuper ad litteram possunt per spinas atque maceriam intelligi corporales munitiones factæ adversus Judæos tempore obsidionum dictarum, ita quod non invenerunt semitas suas, id est modum vel iter effugiendi. Et sequetur amatores suos, id est, cordialiter affectabit auxilium hominum in quibus speravit, videlicet Ægyptiorum tempore obsidionis suæ a Chaldæis. Promisit enim rex Ægypti Sedeciæ, quod auxiliaretur ei contra Chaldæos. Et non apprehendet eos : non enim poterant ei succurrere. Et quæret eos per nuntios ac litteras, et non inveniet.
paras.en: [[2:6|Wherefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because thou hast said, [[2:5|I will go after my lovers|Vadam post amatores meos]], [[2:6|behold, I will hedge up|ecce ego Dominus sepiam]] [Denis reads ‘behold I the Lord will hedge up’], that is, I will fence about and entangle, [[2:6|thy way|viam tuam]], that is, the desire or the action by which thou wert striving to go to thy harmful lovers, [[2:6|with thorns|spinis]], that is, with sorrows and hardships and adversities of many kinds, [[2:6|and I will stop it up with a wall|et sepiam eam maceria]], that is, with a wall or great obstacle, by which she shall be hindered from coming whither she went. [[2:6|and she shall not find her paths|Et semitas suas non inveniet]], that is, she shall not be able to bring her desire into effect. For God did not permit these Jews to obtain the help they hoped for from the gods or the men in whom they trusted, but gave them over to most grievous punishments through the siege of the Chaldeans and of the Romans, so that no one could bring them aid. Moreover, by the thorns and the wall can be understood literally the bodily siege-works made against the Jews at the time of those sieges, so that they did not find their paths, that is, a means or way of escape. [[2:7|And she shall follow after her lovers|Et sequetur amatores suos]], that is, she shall earnestly long for the help of the men in whom she hoped, namely the Egyptians, at the time of her siege by the Chaldeans; for the king of Egypt promised Sedecias that he would help him against the Chaldeans. [[2:7|and shall not overtake them|Et non apprehendet eos]], for they could not come to her aid. [[2:7|and she shall seek them|Et quæret eos]] by messengers and letters, [[2:7|and shall not find|et non inveniet]].

paras.t: Et dicet, necessitate compulsa, juxta illud, Compelle intrare : Vadam spiritualiter de vitiis ad virtutes, de amatoribus vanis ad verum ac infallibilem amatorem, et revertar ad virum meum priorem, id est ad Deum æternum, deserendo bona caduca, et inhærendo bono incommutabili, Deo summo ac omnipotenti, Sponso cœlesti, qui me sibi desponsavit in legis collatione, vel in sanctorum Patriarcharum adoptatione, et promissione eis facta de beneficiis conferendis posteritati eorum; quia bene mihi erat tunc, quando Deo vero adhæsi ac parui, magis quam nunc, dum idolis deservivi, atque humana subsidia exquisivi. Constat enim ex toto decursu veteris Testamenti, quod multo melius successit populo Judæorum, tam in spiritualibus quam in temporalibus bonis, quando divinæ legis observavit præcepta, quam dum idola coluit, vel extranearum nationum postulavit auxilia.
paras.en: [[2:7|and she shall say|Et dicet]], compelled by necessity, according to that saying: [[Luke 14:23|compel them to come in|Compelle intrare]]: [[2:7|I will go|Vadam]], spiritually, from vices to virtues, from vain lovers to the true and unfailing lover, [[2:7|and return to my first husband|et revertar ad virum meum priorem]], that is, to the eternal God, forsaking perishable goods and cleaving to the unchangeable good, God most high and almighty, the heavenly Bridegroom, who espoused me to himself in the giving of the Law, or in the adoption of the holy Patriarchs and the promise made to them of benefits to be bestowed on their posterity; [[2:7|because it was better with me then|quia bene mihi erat tunc]], when I cleaved to the true God and obeyed him, [[2:7|than now|magis quam nunc]], while I have served idols and sought out human help. For it is clear from the whole course of the Old Testament that things went much better for the Jewish people, in spiritual as well as in temporal goods, when it kept the precepts of the divine law, than when it worshipped idols or begged the help of foreign nations.

paras.t: Istud autem, videlicet, Revertar ad virum meum priorem, dixerunt Judæi, saltem aliqui, quando jam viderunt se a Chaldæis mox capiendos. Tunc namque viderunt, quod dii et homines eis nil profuerunt. Propter quod Dei succursum petebant, sed nimis tarde et frustra, quia ex necessitate potius quam ex caritate. Vel si tunc non revertebantur, certum est quod in Chaldæa positi, ad Deum conversi sunt, maxime expletis annis septuaginta, de quibus prædixerat Jeremias. — Huic quoque verbo, Vadam et revertar ad virum meum priorem, simile est quod ait filius prodigus ad extremam perductus inopiam : Quanti mercenarii in domo patris mei abundant panibus, ego autem hic fame pereo! Surgam, et ibo ad patrem meum, etc.
paras.en: Now this, namely, [[2:7|return to my first husband|Revertar ad virum meum priorem]], the Jews said, or at least some of them, when they saw that they were soon to be taken by the Chaldeans. For then they saw that gods and men had been of no profit to them. For this reason they sought God's help, but too late and in vain, because it was out of necessity rather than out of charity. Or if they did not return then, it is certain that, once placed in Chaldea, they were converted to God, above all when the seventy years were fulfilled of which Jeremias had foretold[[Jer 29:10||]]. — Like this saying, [[2:7|I will go, and return to my first husband|Vadam et revertar ad virum meum priorem]], is what the prodigal son says when brought to extreme want: [[Luke 15:17|How many hired servants in my father's house abound with bread, and I here perish with hunger!|Quanti mercenarii in domo patris mei abundant panibus, ego autem hic fame pereo!]] [[Luke 15:18|I will arise and will go to my father|Surgam, et ibo ad patrem meum]], etc.

paras.t: Et hæc mater viperina atque incredula Synagoga nescivit, quia ego dedi ei frumentum et vinum et oleum, id est cibos et potus ac condimenta eorum, quæ pertinent ad naturales divitias. Unde paulo ante adscripsit hæc omnia amatoribus suis seu idolis. Ad tantam equidem mentis cæcitatem venerunt Judæi ante Babylonicam captivitatem, quod divinam providentiam negaverunt. Propterea non putabant sibi a Deo vero collata ea quæ possidebant. De hoc Jeremias et Ezechiel plene loquuntur. Et argentum multiplicavi ei, id est, copiam argenti eis concessi, et aurum, quæ fecerunt Baal, id est, argentum et aurum, quæ eis multiplicavi ut ad honorem meum talibus uterentur, expenderunt in fornicationibus, sacrificiis atque idolis ornaverunt idoli quod dicitur Baal estque deus Sidoniorum ; vel Bel, deus Babyloniorum. Hoc enim idolum ornaverunt argento et auro, et eadem ei immolaverunt. — Denique spiritualiter dedit Deus populo Judæorum frumentum, id est legem, cujus observantia aluit mentem; et vinum, id est veræ hilaritatis materiam seu multiplex gaudium; oleum quoque unctionis ac illustrationis mentalis; argentum, id est eloquentiæ venustatem vel rerum creatarum scientiam; et aurum, id est sapientiam quæ est notitia divinorum; vel aurum, id est Dei amorem, de quo in Apocalypsi scriptum est : Suadeo tibi emere aurum probatum ignitum, ut locuples fias. Hæc bona ac munera Dei, electi Judæi conservabant, et Deo grati fuerunt; quidam vero eorum ea rejecerunt, et totum quod a Deo sortiti fuerunt, converterunt ad idolorum culturam, atque ad cetera mala.
paras.en: [[2:8|And she|Et hæc]], the viperine mother and unbelieving Synagogue, [[2:8|did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil|nescivit, quia ego dedi ei frumentum et vinum et oleum]], that is, foods and drinks and their seasonings, which belong to natural riches. Whence a little before she ascribed all these things to her lovers or idols. Indeed, the Jews came to such blindness of mind before the Babylonian captivity that they denied divine providence; therefore they did not think that what they possessed had been bestowed on them by the true God. Of this Jeremias and Ezechiel speak fully[[Jer 44:15||]]. [[2:8|and multiplied her silver|Et argentum multiplicavi ei]], that is, I granted them abundance of silver, [[2:8|and gold, which they have used in the service of Baal|et aurum, quæ fecerunt Baal]] [literally ‘which they made Baal’], that is, the silver and gold which I multiplied for them so that they might use such things to my honour, they spent on fornications and sacrifices and on idols; they adorned with them the idol which is called Baal, who is the god of the Sidonians, or Bel, the god of the Babylonians [the printed text reads *idoli*, which does not construe; it is taken here as *idolum*]. For they adorned this idol with silver and gold, and offered these same things to it. — Finally, spiritually God gave the Jewish people corn, that is, the Law, the keeping of which nourished the mind; and wine, that is, the matter of true gladness, or manifold joy; also the oil of anointing and of the mind's enlightening; silver, that is, the grace of eloquence or the knowledge of created things; and gold, that is, wisdom, which is the knowledge of divine things; or gold, that is, the love of God, of which it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy of me gold, fire tried, that thou mayest be made rich|Suadeo tibi emere aurum probatum ignitum, ut locuples fias]]. These goods and gifts of God the elect Jews preserved, and were grateful to God; but some of them rejected them, and turned all that they had received from God to the worship of idols and to other evils.

paras.t: Consequenter comminatur Dominus debitam pœnam pro tantis piaculis. Idcirco convertar, per novi effectus operationem, non per mei ipsius mutationem : convertar itaque a pietate clementiæ ad rigorem justitiæ, puniendo quibus diu peperci; et sumam frumentum meum, id est, blada tollam a Judæis, in tempore suo, id est tempore messis, quando jam propter maturitatem apta erant reponi in horreis : et hoc est gravissima pœna, dum tempore maturitatis et messis terræ nascentia auferuntur, et perit labor agricolarum ; vel, In tempore suo, id est tempore præfinito a me; et vinum meum, id est vinum quod contuli eis, auferam, in tempore suo, id est tempore torcularis sive vindemiæ, vel tempore præordinato a me. Hæc Deus abstulit Judæis per tempestates vel hostes, quando a Chaldæis seu aliis vastabantur. Et liberabo lanam meam et linum meum, id est, materiam vestimentorum quæ eis concessi, tollam ab eis, ne ab ingratis et impiis possideantur. Dum enim rationalis creatura abutitur bonis Creatoris, hæc ipsa bona indebitæ servituti subduntur. Idcirco liberari dicuntur, dum ab injustis dominis auferuntur. Quæ lana et linum operiebant ignominiam ejus, id est, idolum populi hujus ornabant. Judæi enim idolatræ, idolum Baal multiplici genere vestium decorabant. Idolum ergo ignominia appellatur, quia hoc erat Judæis ignominiosissimum atque turpissimum, quod relicto Deo patrum suorum, omnipotenti, vero ac summo, idola coluerunt. Superius quoque dictum est, quid spiritualiter per frumentum, vinum, lanam et linum signetur, et quomodo omnia hæc eis spiritualiter sint ablata.
paras.en: Next the Lord threatens the punishment due for such great crimes. [[2:9|Therefore will I return|Idcirco convertar]], by working a new effect, not by any change in myself: I will turn, then, from the tenderness of mercy to the rigour of justice, punishing those whom I have long spared; [[2:9|and take away my corn|et sumam frumentum meum]], that is, I will take the grain from the Jews, [[2:9|in its season|in tempore suo]], that is, at the time of harvest, when because of their ripeness they were already fit to be stored in the barns: and this is a most grievous punishment, when the fruits of the earth are taken away at the time of ripeness and harvest, and the labour of the husbandmen perishes; or, [[2:9|in its season|In tempore suo]], that is, at the time fixed beforehand by me; [[2:9|and my wine|et vinum meum]], that is, the wine which I bestowed on them, I will take away, [[2:9|in its season|in tempore suo]], that is, at the time of the winepress or vintage, or at the time ordained beforehand by me. These things God took from the Jews by storms or enemies, when they were laid waste by the Chaldeans or by others. [[2:9|and I will set at liberty my wool, and my flax|Et liberabo lanam meam et linum meum]], that is, the material for clothing which I granted them I will take from them, so that it may not be possessed by the ungrateful and the wicked. For when the rational creature abuses the goods of the Creator, those goods are subjected to an undue servitude; therefore they are said to be set at liberty when they are taken away from unjust masters. [[2:9|which|Quæ]] wool and flax [[2:9|covered her disgrace|operiebant ignominiam ejus]], that is, which adorned the idol of this people. For the idolatrous Jews decked the idol Baal with many kinds of garments. The idol, then, is called a disgrace, because it was most disgraceful and most shameful for the Jews that, forsaking the God of their fathers, almighty, true and most high, they worshipped idols. What is signified spiritually by the corn, the wine, the wool and the flax, and how all these were spiritually taken from them, has also been said above.

2.title: PROSECUTIO ELUCIDATIONIS HUJUS SECUNDI CAPITULI, AB EO LOCO : ET NUNC REVELABO STULTITIAM EJUS.
2.title_en: Continuation of the explanation of this second chapter, from the place: And now I will lay open her folly.
2.note: Part of this article is lost in the transcription used for this translation (PDF p. 230, printed p. 220: the end of the left column and the whole right column, in the exposition of v. 15); it is marked […].

paras.t: QUONIAM per ea, per quæ quis peccat, punitur, idcirco Dominus subdit : Et nunc, id est tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis, revelabo stultitiam ejus, id est, errorem, seu idololatriam, vel idolum Synagogæ manifestabo, in oculis amatorum ejus, id est Chaldæis vel Ægyptiis, cum quibus Judæi habuerunt aliquando amicitiam. Quum enim Chaldæi, superata Jerusalem, ingrediebantur templum, viderunt quomodo Judæi in templo idola coluerunt, et qualiter decepti fuerunt insipienter in Ægyptiis confidendo. Ægyptii quoque hæc perceperunt, et ita in oculis eorum mentalibus manifestata sunt hæc. Et vir non eruet eam de manu mea, id est, nemo poterit liberare Judæos de vindicta seu potestate, quam exercebo in eis per manus Chaldæorum. Deo enim nullus valet resistere, quemadmodum scriptum est in Job : Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest; et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, fecit.
