But unworthy rulers do the opposite of this, [[2 Tim 3:13|erring, and driving into error|errantes et in errorem mittentes]], [[Matt 15:14|blind, and leaders of the blind|cæci et duces cæcorum]].

6.title: DE MORALITATE HUJUS CAPITULI SEXTI.
6.title_en: On the moral sense of this sixth chapter.

paras.t: QUEMADMODUM itaque Dominus ait in præsentis capituli principio, In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me, et nos debemus in omni tribulatione corporali seu spirituali, in omni tentatione et persecutione oculos ad Deum dirigere, ejusque clementiam implorare, ut vel liberemur, vel patienter feramus et prævaleamus, quemadmodum ait Psalmista : Ad Dominum, quum tribularer, clamavi. Unde secundo Paralipomenon Josaphat ait : In nobis non est tanta fortitudo, ut possimus resistere; sed quum ignoremus quid agere debeamus, hoc solum habemus residui, ut oculos nostros dirigamus ad te. Magnam nobis spem præstant verba Dei, dicentis : Salus populi ego sum; de quacumque tribulatione clamaverint ad me, exaudiam eos. Multis quoque tribulatio est incitamentum consurgendi ad Deum, qui in prosperis extollerentur : in quibus impleretur illud Isaiæ, Sola vexatio dabit intellectum.
paras.en: Just as the Lord says at the beginning of the present chapter, [[6:1|In their affliction they will rise early to me|In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me]], so we too ought, in every tribulation of body or of spirit, in every temptation and persecution, to direct our eyes to God and implore His clemency, that we may either be delivered or bear it patiently and prevail; as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 119:1|In my trouble I cried to the Lord|Ad Dominum, quum tribularer, clamavi]]. Hence in the second book of Paralipomenon Josaphat says: [[2 Par 20:12|as for us we have not strength enough, to be able to resist|In nobis non est tanta fortitudo, ut possimus resistere]]; [[2 Par 20:12|But as we know not what to do, we can only turn our eyes to thee|sed quum ignoremus quid agere debeamus, hoc solum habemus residui, ut oculos nostros dirigamus ad te]]. The words of God give us great hope, when He says: I am the salvation of the people; in whatever tribulation they shall cry to me, I will hear them[[Is 43:1||]][[Ps 36:39||]] [these are the words of the Introit of the Mass of the nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost; the margin gives "Cf. Is. xliii; Ps. xxxvi, 39", passages of like sense]. For many, too, tribulation is a spur to rise up to God, who in prosperity would be lifted up with pride: in them is fulfilled that saying of Isaias, [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand|Sola vexatio dabit intellectum]].

paras.t: Debemus insuper nos invicem cohortari, dicentes, Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum, prout ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus : Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies, ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati. Peccando autem mortaliter, a Deo omnino recedimus. Venialiter vero peccando, ab ipso aliqualiter elongamur, et nisi adsit custodia diligens, ad recessum disponimur.
paras.en: We ought moreover to exhort one another, saying, [[6:1|Come, and let us return to the Lord|Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum]], as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 3:13|exhort one another every day|Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies]], [[Heb 3:13|that none of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin|ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati]]. Now by sinning mortally we depart from God altogether; but by sinning venially we are drawn some way off from Him, and unless a careful watch is kept, we are disposed to depart.

paras.t: Vivificabit nos, per gratiæ suæ infusionem, post duos dies, id est post attritionem et invocationem. Contritionem quippe præcedit attritio, quam sequitur divinæ pietatis imploratio; tuncque Deus videns hominem fecisse quod in se est, influit vitam gratiæ, quæ dirimit mortem culpæ. In die tertia, id est in confessione, quæ attritionem et invocationem consequitur, suscitabit nos perfecte, etiam a reatu totaliter aut partim, secundum quantitatem pudoris, contritionis atque fervoris.
paras.en: [[6:3|He will revive us|Vivificabit nos]], by the infusion of His grace, [[6:3|after two days|post duos dies]], that is, after attrition and prayer. For attrition goes before contrition [attrition being sorrow for sin out of fear of punishment, contrition sorrow out of the love of God], and the imploring of God's mercy follows it; and then God, seeing that the man has done what is in him, pours in the life of grace, which ends the death of guilt. [[6:3|on the third day|In die tertia]], that is, in confession, which follows attrition and prayer, [[6:3|he will raise us up|suscitabit nos]] perfectly, even from the debt of punishment [Latin *reatus*: the liability to punishment that remains after the guilt is forgiven], wholly or in part, according to the measure of our shame, contrition and fervour.

paras.t: Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus. Præter duplicem Christi egressum, in præcedenti articulo positum, est tertius ejus egressus, quo spiritualiter venit ad corda fidelium, de quo ait in Joanne : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Hic ergo egressus præparatus est nobis quasi diluculum seu aurora, ut depellat a nobis obscuritatem peccati, et omne quod saluti animæ adversatur, dummodo mane surgamus ad eum, primo omnium quærentes regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et cum Psalmista dicentes : Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vigilo; itemque cum Isaia, De mane vigilabo ad te. Stat enim ad ostium pulsans. Et veniet quasi imber nobis temporaneus, rorem consolationis et fecunditatis, aquamque sapientiæ salutaris donando, et serotinus terræ, quando transfert nos de fide ad speciem, de merito ad præmium, de imperfecto ad perfectionem, de quibus ait Apostolus : Quum venerit quod perfectum est, evacuabitur quod ex parte est. Unde in Evangelio scriptum est : Quum sero factum esset, dixit dominus vineæ procuratori : Voca operarios, et redde illis mercedem.
paras.en: [[6:3|His going forth is prepared as the morning light|Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus]]. Besides the twofold going forth of Christ set out in the preceding article, there is a third going forth of His, by which He comes spiritually into the hearts of the faithful, of which He says in John: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word. And my Father will love him and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]]. This going forth, then, is prepared for us as the morning light or the dawn, to drive away from us the darkness of sin and all that is against the salvation of the soul, provided that we rise early to Him, seeking first of all [[Matt 6:33|the kingdom of God, and his justice|regnum Dei et justitiam ejus]], and saying with the Psalmist: [[Ps 62:2|O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day|Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vigilo]]; and likewise with Isaias, [[Is 26:9|in the morning early I will watch to thee|De mane vigilabo ad te]]. For He stands at the gate knocking[[Apoc 3:20||]]. [[6:3|and he will come to us as the early|Et veniet quasi imber nobis temporaneus]], giving the dew of consolation and fruitfulness, and [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aquamque sapientiæ salutaris]]; [[6:3|and the latter rain to the earth|et serotinus terræ]], when He brings us over from faith to sight, from merit to reward, from the imperfect to perfection, of which the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 13:10|when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away|Quum venerit quod perfectum est, evacuabitur quod ex parte est]]. Hence it is written in the Gospel: [[Matt 20:8|when evening was come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his steward: Call the labourers and pay them their hire|Quum sero factum esset, dixit dominus vineæ procuratori : Voca operarios, et redde illis mercedem]].

paras.t: Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? quid faciam tibi, Juda? Hæc possunt esse verba clementissimi Dei ad Christianos peccatores, temporalia congregantes, et labiis tantum confitentes, vel aliis vitiis implicitos, quos Deus ad pœnitentiam indesinenter invitat, eorum damnationi velut compatiens. De quo dicit Apostolus, quod vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire. Hinc et Petrus dicit : Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti. Cui consonans Isaias : Propterea, inquit, exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri. Non ergo divitias bonitatis et longanimitatis ejus contemnamus. Mallet enim Christus animarum amator denuo crucifigi, quam sineret quempiam (quantum in se est) condemnari. Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina. Multa enim beneficia tribuit istis Deus, videlicet sacramenta Ecclesiæ. Sed ipsi negligunt semetipsos, et misericordia Dei eis oblata, tanquam nubes matutina, non firmatur nec perseverat in eis. Sed utinam gratia et misericordia nostra comparetur nubi de qua loquitur Isaias : Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, et ingredietur Ægyptum; et rursus, Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant?
paras.en: [[6:4|What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim? what shall I do to thee, O Juda?|Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? quid faciam tibi, Juda?]] These may be the words of the most clement God to Christian sinners who gather up temporal things and confess with their lips only[[Matt 15:8||]], or are entangled in other vices, whom God unceasingly invites to penance, as though suffering with them in their damnation. Of which the Apostle says that He [[1 Tim 2:4|will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire]]. Hence Peter too says: The Lord [[2 Pet 3:9|dealeth patiently for your sake, not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]]. In agreement with whom Isaias: [[Is 30:18|Therefore|Propterea]], he says, [[Is 30:18|the Lord waiteth that he may have mercy on you|exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri]]. Let us not then despise [[Rom 2:4|the riches of his goodness|divitias bonitatis]] and His longsuffering. For Christ, the lover of souls, would rather be crucified again than let anyone be condemned (as far as lies in Him). [[6:4|your mercy is as a morning cloud|Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina]]. For God bestows many benefits on these, namely the sacraments of the Church. But they neglect themselves, and the mercy of God offered them, like a morning cloud, is not made firm nor does it last in them. But would that our grace and mercy might be likened to the cloud of which Isaias speaks: [[Is 19:1|Behold the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud, and will enter into Egypt|Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, et ingredietur Ægyptum]]; and again, [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant]]?

paras.t: Quia misericordiam volui, et non sacrificium. Ex hoc docemur, quam benignos, pios et compassivos, ad ignoscendumque faciles, et ad tribuendum ac succurrendum paratos esse oporteat, ut alter alterius onera portemus, et tales exhibeamus nos proximis nostris, qualem cupimus Deum esse nobis. Propter quod ad Ephesios scribit præcipitque Apostolus : Omnis amaritudo et indignatio et ira et clamor tollatur a vobis ; estote vero invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis. Salomon quoque : Qui pronus est ad misericordiam, benedicetur; et iterum ait, Facere misericordiam, plus placet Deo, quam victimæ. Hæc verba Osee allegat Christus contra Pharisæos apud Matthæum, dum ait : Euntes discite quid sit, Misericordiam volo et non sacrificium.
paras.en: [[6:6|For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice|Quia misericordiam volui, et non sacrificium]]. From this we are taught how kind, loving and compassionate, how ready to forgive, and how prompt to give and to help we ought to be, that we may bear one another's burdens[[Gal 6:2||]], and show ourselves to our neighbours such as we desire God to be to us. For this reason the Apostle writes and commands the Ephesians: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour and blasphemy be put away from you|Omnis amaritudo et indignatio et ira et clamor tollatur a vobis]]; [[Eph 4:32|be ye kind one to another: merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ|estote vero invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis]]. Solomon too: [[Prov 22:9|He that is inclined to mercy, shall be blessed|Qui pronus est ad misericordiam, benedicetur]]; and again he says, [[Prov 21:3|To do mercy|Facere misericordiam]] [[Prov 21:3|pleaseth the Lord more than victims|plus placet Deo, quam victimæ]]. These words of Osee Christ brings forward against the Pharisees in Matthew, when He says: [[Matt 9:13|Go then and learn what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice|Euntes discite quid sit, Misericordiam volo et non sacrificium]].

paras.t: Et scientiam Dei plus quam holocausta. Sanctum ergo et acceptissimum Deo est, studio sacræ Scripturæ insistere, sic tamen ut modus servetur, et utiliora non omittantur. Unde dicit Hieronymus : Semper in manibus tuis sacra sit lectio, tenenti tibi codicem somnus subrepat, et cadentem faciem pagina sancta suscipiat; ama scientiam sanctarum Scripturarum, et vitia carnis non amabis. Verumtamen hæc salutaris scientia Dei, interdum pura oratione et immaculatæ conversationis munditia melius atque felicius impetratur. Propter quod Jacobus ait : Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei.
paras.en: [[6:6|and the knowledge of God more than holocausts|Et scientiam Dei plus quam holocausta]]. It is therefore holy and most acceptable to God to apply oneself to the study of Holy Scripture, yet so that measure is kept and more useful things are not left undone. Hence Jerome says: Let holy reading be always in your hands; let sleep steal upon you as you hold the book, and let the sacred page receive your face as it falls; love the knowledge of the holy Scriptures, and you will not love the vices of the flesh. Yet this saving knowledge of God is sometimes better and more happily obtained by pure prayer and by the cleanness of a spotless life. For this reason James says: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not. And it shall be given him|Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei]].

paras.t: Galaad civitas operantium idolum. Galaad interpretatur, transmigratio testimonii : sicque designat perversos prælatos, impiosque doctores seu prædicatores, qui testimonia Scripturarum transferunt in abusionem et voluptatem carnalem, in omnibus quæ operantur propria commoda exquirentes. Isti sunt civitas operantium idolum propriæ adinventionis, non voluntatem divinæ jussionis. Suntque præterea velut fauces latronum, quoniam subditorum bona consumunt, eosque malis exemplis et negligentia ac tepore spiritualiter strangulant et occidunt. Et sunt participes sacerdotum iniquorum, qui pergentes in via virtutum de Sichem, id est opere bono, ad Jerusalem, id est internæ pacis contemplationem, interficiunt, retrahendo eos a bono, atque in vitia inducendo.
paras.en: [[6:8|Galaad is a city of workers of idols|Galaad civitas operantium idolum]]. Galaad is interpreted "the passing over of testimony": and so it signifies perverse prelates and impious doctors or preachers, who turn the testimonies of the Scriptures over to abuse and fleshly pleasure, seeking their own advantage in all that they do. These are the city of workers of the idol of their own invention, not of the will of God's command. And moreover they are [[6:9|like the jaws of highway robbers|velut fauces latronum]], since they consume the goods of their subjects, and by their bad example, their negligence and their lukewarmness spiritually strangle and kill them. And they are partakers of the wicked priests, who murder those that go in the way of virtue from Sichem, that is, from good works, to Jerusalem, that is, to the contemplation of inward peace, drawing them back from good and leading them into vice.

paras.t: In domo Israel vidi horrendum. Horrendum plane est, considerare aut dicere quam immanissima vitia inveniantur jam in Ecclesia Dei, præsertim in his qui spiritualibus deputati videntur, et de Ecclesiæ bonis sustentantur.
paras.en: [[6:10|I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel|In domo Israel vidi horrendum]]. Horrible indeed it is to consider or to tell what monstrous vices are found now in the Church of God, above all in those who seem to be set apart for spiritual things and are maintained from the goods of the Church.

paras.t: Postremo, quod in isto capitulo dictum est, Quia ipse cepit et sanabit nos, quidam ad litteram sic exponunt : Ipse Christus cepit, id est, apprehendit nos, eo modo quo ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus, Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit : quia videlicet ex semine Abrahæ naturam assumpsit humanam. Hinc et David fatetur : Misit de summo, et accepit me. Quamvis autem expositio ista sit vera, non tamen ad propositum esse censetur, quia pro eo quod nostra translatio continet, Ipse cepit, in Hebræo et in translatione Septuaginta interpretam habetur, Ipse rapuit : et secundum hoc, littera ista exposita est præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: Lastly, what is said in this chapter, [[6:2|he hath taken us, and he will heal us|Quia ipse cepit et sanabit nos]], some expound literally thus: Christ Himself hath taken, that is, laid hold of us, in the way in which the Apostle says to the Hebrews, [[Heb 2:16|nowhere doth he take hold of the angels: but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold|Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit]]: because, namely, He took human nature of the seed of Abraham. Hence David too confesses: [[Ps 17:17|He sent from on high, and took me|Misit de summo, et accepit me]]. But although this exposition is true, it is not thought to be to the purpose, because where our translation has "He hath taken", in the Hebrew and in the translation of the Seventy interpreters there stands "He hath snatched away": and according to this the letter was expounded in the preceding article [Art. XIII, Denis's literal exposition of this chapter].

7.title: DECLARATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM CAPITULI SEPTIMI.
7.title_en: Moral explanation of the same seventh chapter.

paras.t: De Israel et Ephraim ac Samaria possumus loqui dupliciter: primo, secundum nominum interpretationem; secundo, quoad conversationis illorum maneriem. Quoniam ergo vita decem tribuum, scilicet Ephraim et Israel, pessima fuit, postquam recesserunt de domo David, quia ex tunc idola coluerunt; ideo per eos significantur quandoque inobedientes Christiani, hæretici, ceterique perversi. Loquendo autem de Israel secundum nominis interpretationem, quæ est, Vir videns Deum, non designat proprie nisi fideles et bonos. Ephraim vero quod interpretatur incrementum, significare potest hoc modo et bonos et malos: secundum quod aliqui crescunt in verbis bonis ac spiritualibus, alii in rebus malis, inutilibus sive superfluis. Verumtamen in præsenti loco Israel et Ephraim accipiuntur in malo, secundum quod populus ille pravissimus erat.
paras.en: Of Israel and Ephraim and Samaria we can speak in two ways: first, according to the interpretation of the names; secondly, as regards the manner of their way of life. Since, then, the life of the ten tribes, namely of Ephraim and Israel, was very wicked after they departed from the house of David, because from that time they worshipped idols, they sometimes signify disobedient Christians, heretics and other perverse men. But speaking of Israel according to the interpretation of the name, which is "a man seeing God", it properly designates only the faithful and the good. Ephraim, however, which is interpreted "increase", can in this way signify both the good and the wicked: inasmuch as some increase in good and spiritual words, others in things that are evil, useless or superfluous. In the present place, however, Israel and Ephraim are taken in a bad sense, inasmuch as that people was most depraved.

paras.t: Est itaque tropologicus intellectus: Quum ego Christus post resurrectionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem, sanare vellem Israel, id est populum Ecclesiæ, christianum sola fide ac nomine, qui fide informi speculantur divina; revelata est iniquitas Ephraim, id est, peccata principum ac prælatorum plebis christianæ eruperunt et propalata sunt. Hi enim dicuntur Ephraim, quasi in temporalibus concrescentes, et quoniam præsident aliis, quemadmodum reges decem tribuum communiter de tribu Ephraim exstiterunt. Et malitia Samariæ. Per Samariam decem tribuum metropolim, figurantur principales in domibus prælatorum ac principum, qui communiter primo adhærent iniquitatibus præsidentium. Hi itaque prælati ac principes mali cum suis domesticis, sæpe impediunt subditorum salutem, dum eos blandimentis, comminationibus, vel exemplis trahunt ad culpam, per quam gratiæ Dei obicem ponunt, ne illustrentur atque curentur. Unde apud Jeremiam legitur: Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Summo ergo humillimoque affectu exorandus est Deus, ut præstet bonum prælatum, principemque condignum.
paras.en: The tropological sense, then, is this: [[7:1|When|Quum]] I, Christ, after the resurrection and the sending of the Holy Ghost, [[7:1|would have healed Israel|sanare vellem Israel]], that is, the people of the Church, Christian by faith and name alone, who contemplate divine things with an unformed faith [that is, faith without charity, which does not give life to the soul], [[7:1|the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered|revelata est iniquitas Ephraim]], that is, the sins of the princes and prelates of the Christian people broke out and were made public. For these are called Ephraim, as growing great in temporal things, and because they preside over others, just as the kings of the ten tribes commonly came from the tribe of Ephraim. [[7:1|and the wickedness of Samaria|Et malitia Samariæ]]. By Samaria, the capital of the ten tribes, are figured the chief men in the households of prelates and princes, who are commonly the first to cleave to the iniquities of those who preside. These wicked prelates and princes, then, with their households, often hinder the salvation of their subjects, while by flatteries, threats or examples they draw them into sin, by which they put an obstacle to the grace of God, so that they are not enlightened and healed. Hence we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly, and have not sought the Lord|Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. God, then, is to be entreated with the deepest and humblest affection to grant a good prelate and a worthy prince.

paras.t: Dum ergo superiores subditorum salutem impediunt, impletur quod subditur: Et fur ingressus est spolians. Per quem intelligi potest diabolus, qui tunc corda ingreditur subditorum, et spiritualibus eos bonis destituit, secundum quod ait Salvator in Evangelio: Venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde ipsorum, ne credentes salvi fiant. Hic quoque diabolus est, latrunculus foris, animas strangulans, atque in caliginoso aere habitans, et in omni itinere nostro nobis insidians. Vel nomine furis datur intelligi omnis seductor occultus, simulator et callidus: qui mentem lupinam veste ovina abscondens, multos subvertit, spoliat et occidit, idcirco et latrunculus appellatur. De talibus ait Salvator: Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces. Et revera omnis superior sibi commissos negligens aut subvertens, fur dici potest et latro, de cujus manu sanguis pereuntium quæritur.
paras.en: While, then, superiors hinder the salvation of their subjects, what follows is fulfilled: [[7:1|and the thief is come in to steal|Et fur ingressus est spolians]]. By him may be understood the devil, who then enters the hearts of the subjects and strips them of spiritual goods, according to what the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 8:12|the devil cometh and taketh the word out of their heart, lest believing they should be saved|Venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde ipsorum, ne credentes salvi fiant]]. This devil too is [[7:1|the robber is without|latrunculus foris]], strangling souls, dwelling in the dark air, and lying in wait for us on every road we take. Or by the name of thief is meant every hidden seducer, dissembling and crafty, who, hiding a wolfish mind under sheep's clothing, overthrows, despoils and kills many; and for this reason he is also called a robber. Of such the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]] And indeed every superior who neglects or overthrows those committed to him may be called a thief and a robber, at whose hand the blood of those who perish is required.

paras.t: Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ: id est, ne perversi et impœnitentes dicant se puniri propter antiqua sua vel aliorum peccata, per pœnitentiam vel castigationem deleta; jam nunc quotidie tot nova peccata addunt veteribus, quod recentibus vitiis circumdantur et puniri merentur, nec possunt se excusare. De talibus dicit Apostolus: Impii proficient in pejus; et Psalmista, Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum, transierunt in affectum cordis.
paras.en: [[7:2|And lest they may say in their hearts, that I remember all their wickedness: their own devices now have beset them about|Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ]]: that is, lest the perverse and impenitent say that they are punished for their own old sins or those of others, which have been blotted out by penance or chastisement, even now they daily add so many new sins to the old that they are beset by fresh vices and deserve to be punished, and cannot excuse themselves. Of such the Apostle says: The wicked [[2 Tim 3:13|shall grow worse and worse|proficient in pejus]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 72:7|Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: they have passed into the affection of the heart.|Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum, transierunt in affectum cordis]]

paras.t: Coram facie mea factæ sunt. Hoc est quod fertur in Psalmo: Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Apud Job quoque dicitur: Deus novit hominum vanitatem, et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat? Maxima nobis est ratio abstinendi a culpa, quod Deo præsente, intuente ac judicante, agimus intus et foris quidquid egerimus. Ideo enim ait vir sanctus: Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo. Præterea, quam vehementer id pertinet ad omnipotentis Dei irreverentiam, quod amplius humanum quam divinum veremur adspectum; quod Deo attendente audemus cogitare quod coram hominibus non audemus exprimere; quod soli facimus opus Dei negligentius, quam faceremus illud si honesti hominis adesset persona! Semper ergo pensemus ac honoremus præsentiam atque intuitum majestatis divinæ, dicentes ad Creatorem: Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper.
paras.en: [[7:2|they have been done before my face|Coram facie mea factæ sunt]]. This is what is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:6|my offences are not hidden from thee|Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxviii, 6; the words are Ps 68:6]. In Job also it is said: God [[Job 11:11|knoweth the vanity of men, and when he seeth iniquity, doth he not consider it?|novit hominum vanitatem, et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat?]] The greatest reason we have for abstaining from sin is that whatever we do, within and without, we do with God present, looking on and judging. For this is why the holy man says: [[Ps 118:168|I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies: because all my ways are in thy sight.|Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo.]] Moreover, how gravely it touches on irreverence toward almighty God that we fear the sight of man more than that of God; that with God attending we dare to think what we do not dare to utter before men; that when alone we do the work of God more negligently than we would if a respectable man were present! Let us therefore always weigh and honour the presence and the gaze of the divine majesty, saying to the Creator: [[Ps 18:15|the meditation of my heart always in thy sight|meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper]].

paras.t: In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, et in mendaciis suis principes. Sic subditi dum majorum suorum impiæ voluntati assentiunt, eorumque actus perversos approbant et sequuntur, lætificant eos. Quemadmodum enim boni prælati ac principes de subditorum profectu præcipue gaudent, dicente Joanne in tertia sua Canonica, Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes; sic præsidentes indigni jucundantur in his qui ipsorum conformantur erroribus seu peccatis.
paras.en: [[7:3|They have made the king glad with their wickedness: and the princes with their lies.|In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, et in mendaciis suis principes.]] So subjects, when they assent to the impious will of their superiors and approve and follow their perverse acts, make them glad. For just as good prelates and princes rejoice above all in the progress of their subjects, as John says in his third canonical Epistle, [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes]], so unworthy rulers take delight in those who conform themselves to their errors or sins.

paras.t: Omnes isti inepti præsidentes, sunt adulterantes carnaliter aut spiritualiter. Quo contra dicit Apostolus: Non enim sumus sicut plurimi, adulterantes verbum Dei, sed ex sinceritate. Quasi clibanus succensus a coquente, sic inflammati sunt igne libidinis aliorumque vitiorum. Jam videmus quomodo in clericis regnent carnalia vitia, et qui ad ampliorem obligantur munditiam, turpius inquinantur. Quievit paululum civitas a commixtione, donec fermentaretur totum: id est, populus istis indignis prælatis subjectus, successive infectus est, et primo quasi per blandimenta attractus, donec tandem omnino subversus est. Paulatim enim malum invalescit. Idcirco principiis est obstandum, ne parva scintilla universam silvam incendat. Siquidem quod inolitum fuerit, non faciliter emendatur.
paras.en: [[7:4|They are all|Omnes]] these unfit rulers [[7:4|adulterers|sunt adulterantes]], carnally or spiritually. Against which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 2:17|For we are not as many, adulterating the word of God: but with sincerity|Non enim sumus sicut plurimi, adulterantes verbum Dei, sed ex sinceritate]]. [[7:4|like an oven heated by the baker|Quasi clibanus succensus a coquente]], so are they inflamed with the fire of lust and of other vices. We see now how carnal vices reign among clerics, and those who are bound to greater purity are the more foully defiled. [[7:4|the city rested a little from the mingling|Quievit paululum civitas a commixtione]], [[7:4|till the whole was leavened|donec fermentaretur totum]]: that is, the people subject to these unworthy prelates was infected little by little, and at first drawn as if by flatteries, until at last it was utterly overthrown. For evil grows strong by degrees. Therefore beginnings must be resisted, lest a small spark set the whole forest ablaze. For what has become ingrained is not easily amended.

paras.t: Dies regis nostri. Solent majores in sæculo isto certos præfigere dies ad vacandum spectaculis, vanitatibus seu conviviis; et in illis diebus plebs illis applaudens, vanaque festa ac impia opera peragens, dicit: Dies regis nostri, id est, iste est dies superioris rectorisque nostri, in quo statuit ista quæ agimus, esse agenda. Cœperunt principes furere, id est igne concupiscentiæ inflammari, usumque rationis amittere, et bestialiter se habere, a vino, in quo est luxuria. Nempe in his qui carnem suam nutriunt delicate, vitia copiosius provocantur, et motus libidinosi exsurgunt, ita ut more furentium, impetum passionum sectentur. Extendit manum suam cum illusoribus: id est, impius dominator et pastor subditis sibi vane applaudentibus cooperatur, consentit et commiscetur.
paras.en: [[7:5|The day of our king|Dies regis nostri]]. The great ones of this world are wont to fix certain days for giving themselves to shows, vanities or banquets; and on those days the common people, applauding them and carrying out vain feasts and impious works, say: [[7:5|The day of our king|Dies regis nostri]], that is, this is the day of our superior and ruler, on which he has decreed that these things which we do are to be done. [[7:5|the princes began to be mad|Cœperunt principes furere]], that is, to be inflamed with the fire of concupiscence, to lose the use of reason and to behave like beasts, [[7:5|with wine|a vino]], [[Eph 5:18|wherein is luxury|in quo est luxuria]]. For in those who nourish their flesh delicately, vices are more abundantly stirred up and lustful motions arise, so that like madmen they follow the onrush of the passions. [[7:5|he stretched out his hand with scorners|Extendit manum suam cum illusoribus]]: that is, the impious lord and shepherd works together with his subjects who vainly applaud him, consents to them and mingles with them.

paras.t: Quia applicuerunt quasi clibanum cor suum, id est, prompto animo consenserunt consilio præsidentis; tota nocte, id est durante vitiorum caligine, dormivit, id est, in voluptate et impia securitate quievit, coquens eos, id est, præsidens subditos igne pravitatis indurans, quia non præest in sollicitudine, neque attendit quam districtam ab eo Christus exigit rationem. Si enim unusquisque nostrum, secundum apostolicum documentum, debeat cum metu, timore ac tremore sui ipsius operari salutem: cum quanto metu et cura oportet prælatum sibi aliisque providere, cui tanto gravius instat periculum, quanto pluribus præest? Sed, heu! hoc multi non ponderant, de quibus Isaias inducit: Speculatores cæci, videntes vana et dormientes.
paras.en: [[7:6|Because they have applied their heart like an oven|Quia applicuerunt quasi clibanum cor suum]], that is, they consented with a ready mind to the counsel of the one who presides; [[7:6|all the night|tota nocte]], that is, while the darkness of vices lasts, [[7:6|he slept|dormivit]], that is, he rested in pleasure and impious security, [[7:6|baking them|coquens eos]], that is, the one who presides hardening his subjects with the fire of depravity, because he does not rule [[Rom 12:8|with carefulness|in sollicitudine]], nor considers how strict an account Christ demands of him. For if each of us, according to the Apostle's teaching, must work out his own salvation with dread, fear and trembling[[Phil 2:12||]], with how much dread and care must a prelate provide for himself and for others, on whom the danger presses the more heavily the more men he rules over? But alas, many do not weigh this; of them Isaias says: [[Is 56:10|His watchmen are all blind|Speculatores cæci]], [[Is 56:10|seeing vain things, sleeping|videntes vana et dormientes]].

paras.t: Omnes calefacti sunt igne vitiorum, et devoraverunt judices suos, id est, frequenter persequuntur eos a quibus juste et caritative reprehenduntur. Non enim amat pestilens corripientem. Omnes reges eorum ceciderunt. Inefficaces namque aliorum rectores toties cadunt, quoties peccant, quia peccatum ruina est a rectitudine rationis, a statu virtutis, ab erectione mentis in Deum.
paras.en: [[7:7|They were all heated|Omnes calefacti sunt]] with the fire of vices, [[7:7|and have devoured their judges|et devoraverunt judices suos]], that is, they often persecute those by whom they are justly and charitably rebuked. For the corrupt man loveth not him that reproveth him. [[7:7|all their kings have fallen|Omnes reges eorum ceciderunt]]. For ineffectual rulers of others fall as often as they sin, since sin is a fall from the rectitude of reason, from the state of virtue, from the uplifting of the mind to God.

paras.t: Ephraim, id est præsidentes indigne, in populis ipse commiscebatur, id est, vulgo assimilantur in vili conversatione (quemadmodum dictum est: Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos), quum tamen in Isaia dicatur: Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit. Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, qui non reversatur. Sic omnis impœnitens, qui non excutit se a pulveribus terrenæ affectionis, sed jugiter jacet in uno latere, rebus caducis atque carnalibus inhærendo, est velut subcinericius panis, qui non vertitur in alteram partem. Verum qui audit Apostolum, Quæ sursum sunt quærite; et Joannem, Agite dignos fructus pœnitentiæ: non est hujuscemodi panis sic sordidatus, sed panis mundus, de quo fatur Apostolus: Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, omnes qui de uno pane et de uno calice participamus.
paras.en: [[7:8|Ephraim himself|Ephraim]], that is, those who preside unworthily, [[7:8|is mixed among the nations|in populis ipse commiscebatur]], that is, they become like the common people in a base way of life (as it is said: [[Osee 4:9|there shall be like people like priest|Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]]), whereas in Isaias it is said: [[Is 32:8|the prince will devise such things as are worthy of a prince|Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit]]. [[7:8|Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes, that is not turned|Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, qui non reversatur]]. So every impenitent man, who does not shake himself free of the dust of earthly affection but lies continually on one side, cleaving to perishable and carnal things, is like bread baked under the ashes that is not turned over to the other side. But he who hears the Apostle, [[Col 3:1|seek the things that are above|Quæ sursum sunt quærite]], and John, [[Luke 3:8|Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of penance|Agite dignos fructus pœnitentiæ]], is not bread of this kind, so soiled, but clean bread, of which the Apostle speaks: [[1 Cor 10:17|we, being many, are one bread, one body: all that partake of one bread|Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, omnes qui de uno pane et de uno calice participamus]] [Denis adds "and of one chalice"].

paras.t: Comederunt alieni robur ejus. Hoc fit, dum subversores et dæmones spiritualium bonorum vigore nos privant, ita ut vitiis tanquam effeminati vincamur, nec hostibus animæ reluctemur. Quo contra monet Apostolus ad Ephesios: Confortamini in Domino et in potentia virtutis ejus; induite armaturam Dei, ut possitis stare adversus insidias diabolo. Jacobus quoque: Resistite (inquit) diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. Et ipse nescivit, id est, hanc suam calamitatem, dejectionem, depauperationem non pensavit, nec doluit. Sic multi paulatim evacuantur ac decidunt, nec attendunt: quia et spiritualia dona faciliter, et interdum imperceptibiliter, amittuntur. Sunt insuper aliqui qui adeo infirmantur, quod ægre ferunt, si eis dicatur quod a pristino fervore dilapsi sunt. Unde in Apocalypsi Dominus loquitur: Quomodo dicis, Quia dives sum, quum sis pauper, cæcus et nudus, miser et miserabilis? Memento itaque unde excideris, et pœnitentiam age. Sed et cani effusi sunt in eo, id est, usque in finem vitæ perstiterunt in malo.
paras.en: [[7:9|Strangers have devoured his strength|Comederunt alieni robur ejus]]. This happens when seducers and demons deprive us of the vigour of spiritual goods, so that we are overcome by vices as if unmanned, and do not fight back against the enemies of the soul. Against this the Apostle warns the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:10|be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of his power|Confortamini in Domino et in potentia virtutis ejus]]; [[Eph 6:11|Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil|induite armaturam Dei, ut possitis stare adversus insidias diabolo]]. James also: [[Jas 4:7|resist|Resistite]] (he says) [[Jas 4:7|the devil: and he will fly from you|diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. [[7:9|and he knew it not|Et ipse nescivit]], that is, he did not weigh this calamity of his, his downfall and impoverishment, nor grieve over it. So many are emptied little by little and fall away, and do not notice it: for spiritual gifts are lost easily, and sometimes imperceptibly. There are, moreover, some so weak that they take it ill if they are told that they have fallen away from their former fervour. Hence the Lord says in the Apocalypse: How sayest thou, [[Apoc 3:17|I am rich|dives sum]], when thou art [[Apoc 3:17|poor and blind and naked|pauper, cæcus et nudus]], [[Apoc 3:17|wretched and miserable|miser et miserabilis]]? [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance|Memento itaque unde excideris, et pœnitentiam age]]. [[7:9|yea, grey hairs also are spread about upon him|Sed et cani effusi sunt in eo]], that is, they persisted in evil to the end of their life.

paras.t: Et factus est Ephraim, id est prælati vel in temporalibus fecundati, quasi columba seducta: quia nec propriam, nec gregis sibi commissi damnationem et excæcationem attendunt. Isti invocant humana præsidia, quæ per Ægyptum et Assyrios designantur, sed Dominus apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum. Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me. Æternaliter enim peribunt, nisi pœniteant. Vastantur quoque ab invisibilibus hostibus hæretici, qui Scripturam pervertunt, aut loquuntur contra Christum mendacia.
paras.en: [[7:11|And Ephraim is become|Et factus est Ephraim]], that is, prelates, or those made fruitful in temporal things, [[7:11|as a dove that is decoyed|quasi columba seducta]]: for they do not heed the damnation and blinding either of themselves or of the flock committed to them. These call upon human help, which is signified by Egypt and the Assyrians; but the Lord [[Job 5:13|catcheth the wise in their craftiness|apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum]] [Denis has "the crafty" for "the wise"]. [[7:13|Woe to them, for they have departed from me|Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me]]. For they will perish eternally unless they do penance[[Luke 13:5||]]. Heretics too, who pervert Scripture or speak lies against Christ, are wasted by invisible enemies.

paras.t: Super triticum et vinum ruminabant. Hoc competit his qui post dominici corporis et sanguinis sumptionem crapulose viventes, usque ad ructum implentur.
paras.en: [[7:14|they have thought upon wheat and wine|Super triticum et vinum ruminabant]] [ruminabant, literally "they chewed the cud", which Denis takes up with the belching that follows]. This fits those who, after receiving the Lord's body and blood, live in gluttony and are filled until they belch.

paras.t: Postremo, quomodo sequentia beneficia Dei sint Christianis impensa, et qualiter ipsi vitia quæ subduntur, committant, ex dictis facillime patet.
paras.en: Lastly, how the benefits of God that follow have been bestowed on Christians, and how they commit the vices that are added, is very easily seen from what has been said.
